Milan lost 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros as the Hungarians kept pace with Bournemouth, maintaining their 100% record in Europe.

Haiti international Lenny Joseph struck twice in the second half at San Siro to earn Ferencvaros a deserved win over the seven-time European champions despite having Bamidele Yusuf sent off.

Milan are languishing outside the top 24 with just three points at the halfway stage of the league phase. “I won’t give up on this competition. As long as we’re not mathematically out of it, we’ll keep fighting in this competition, just as we do in the others,” Milan’s coach, Ruben Amorim, said.

In Germany, Marseille earned their first three points of the competition thanks to a stunning solo effort from Amine Gouiri after a largely uneventful contest against Bayer Leverkusen. The forward broke the deadlock in the 77th minute, collecting the ball near halfway before ‌surging past defenders and firing a right-footed shot into the net.

Juventus prevailed 2-1 at AZ Alkmaar, with Teun Koopmeiners opening the scoring against a team captained by his brother Peer in the 19th minute. The ​Dutch midfielder swept home a first-time finish after Randal Kolo Muani beat his marker down the right and cut the ball back to the edge of the area.

Kolo Muani doubled Juventus’s lead eight minutes before half-time, punishing an error forced by the visitors’ high press before cutting inside and drilling a low shot into the far corner. Mexx Meerdink pulled one back late on but AZ ⁠could not find an equaliser.

Juventus are fifth, level on 10 points with Union Saint Gilloise ​and Olympiacos.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye?

The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back.

At the 2022 World Cup, Fernando Santos belatedly took the decision to leave Ronaldo out for the last-16 tie against Switzerland. Portugal suddenly had a fluency and fluidity they had lacked for years and the player who had replaced Ronaldo, Gonçalo Ramos, scored a hat-trick. That seemed incontrovertible evidence the end was upon Ronaldo, or at least his role might become that of an impact substitute.

But even in the final minutes of that game, half the crowd were chanting for Ronaldo. Some, perhaps, were Portuguese fans but many were tourists. They didn’t care much about the result or who went through, they just wanted to see the famous man do the famous thing. Near the end, he scored a goal that was obviously offside. He knew it was offside, but he also knew what his public wanted. So he did the “Siuuuu …” celebration and was rewarded with the biggest cheer of the night. This was like seeing late-period Elvis in Las Vegas: it didn’t matter he was no longer the singer he had been, he was still Elvis. It’s just that Elvis wasn’t also carrying Portugal’s World Cup hopes on his rhinestoned shoulders.

When a player has such celebrity status, when he is still somehow the show no matter how sluggish his movements, making that decision on when to quit must become even harder. And Ronaldo, with his status as Portugal’s greatest soft-power export, also became a political issue. A cabinet minister publicly said he couldn’t be dropped because of how much revenue he generated and what he meant for Portugal’s brand. Portugal is not a country replete with global superstars.

View image in fullscreen Cristiano Ronaldo shows his frustration in the Nations League game against and Wales in September – which has turned out to be his last for Portugal. Photograph: Patrícia de Melo Moreira/AFP/Getty Images

Quick Guide 'Thank you, idol': reaction to Ronaldo's international retirement Show Portuguese Football Federation "Every drop of sweat, every decisive goal, and every captain’s arm-band he wore with honour on the field reflected his unconditional love ⁠for our jersey. His dedication ⁠and his legacy ​transcend the four lines of the field. Ronaldo has raised Portugal’s profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for ⁠many of us, he is the greatest player of all time! …" Al-Nassr (Ronaldo's current club) "It’s not just a chapter – it’s history you’ve shaped. You’re an icon to the entire world, not ⁠just Portugal. Portugal is in your heart, and you are in the hearts of the world. A page ​has turned, but there is still history left ‌for us to write together at ‌your home, Al-Nassr." Manchester United (one of Ronaldo's former clubs) "Congratulations on an incredible international career." Bruno Fernandes (Portugal and Manchester United) "Thank ‌you for the inspiration. It was a privilege to be able to share great moments with our national team alongside my childhood idol." Diogo Dalot (Portugal and Manchester United) "They don’t know that dreams are a constant in life … Portugal’s history tells us that we are a people who have never accepted limits, unafraid of uncharted seas or weathering storms. We were and are shaped by achievements, sacrifices, tears, and sweat … ‌By dreams that seem impossible – until someone has the courage to make them a reality. You did it. You made us believe, dream, and achieve! A legacy that will be remembered ​not only for the trophies or the goals, but also for the path you paved for all those who came after you. Your passion and determination to represent our country is something I’ll never forget and that will stay with me forever. I’m immensely proud of everything you’ve done for our national team! Thank you, idol." Pepe (Former Portugal and Real Madrid defender) "It was more than just soccer. Thanks for everything, Cris." Gianni Infantino, Fifa president "Few players have ever ​touched the heart of football fans ​around the world quite like Cristiano. A career defined by extraordinary talent, relentless determination and ​an unwavering desire to ‌push the boundaries ​of what is possible … Cristiano has ​achieved milestones that may never be matched but his greatest legacy goes far beyond records, trophies and goals … Thank you, Cristiano, for the passion, the unforgettable moments and the immense contribution you have made to our beautiful game proudly wearing the 'Selecao' shirt. Your international career will forever be part of football’s history." Reuters Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Ronaldo hung around at Euro 2024, weeping after missing a penalty against Slovenia, the magnitude of his fame and ego warping perception so everything became about him, no matter how many other hugely gifted players were in that squad. And implausibly he was still doing it at the World Cup this summer: gumming the mechanisms, constantly demanding the ball, occasionally drifting out to the left to get in Rafael Leão’s way. At one point against Spain in what turns out to have been his final World Cup game, Ronaldo was released on the break but, lacking pace, ended up having to turn back and play the ball to his full-back, the opportunity gone. There was something almost painful about seeing a player once so explosive reduced to this.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There needed to be some sort of intervention. This generation of Portuguese players, who really should be challenging for major honours and not just the Nations League, could not continue to struggle on with such an albatross around their necks. It came from Jorge Jesus, the admirably forthright 72-year-old national coach, who was appointed after the World Cup. He didn’t bring Ronaldo off the bench in the second half of a tight game Portugal ended up winning against Norway. Ronaldo insisted he had been promised minutes – but even if there had been an agreement, it would be absurd to refuse a coach the capacity to adapt to circumstance – and stormed out of the camp, an indication perhaps of how his self-regard had come to distort his judgment.

And, assuming this retirement isn’t some sort of power play to force Jesus out, that is where it ended, with a €255 (£212) fine and 30-day ban over a period in which Portugal had no games. Ronaldo will go back to the Saudi Pro League to continue his pursuit of a 1,000th goal. He has been an extraordinary player. He will be remembered as an all-time great, vying with Eusébio as the greatest Portugal player of all time, but his legacy is undoubtedly tainted by this protracted farewell, by the sense that a player who at his best could win games single-handed, came by the end to be a burden to his national team. His has been a great career, but it would have been greater had it been a little shorter.

Sports.title: Scott Parker’s dramatic West Ham return leaves him struggling for words
Sports.content:
Three days in and Scott Parker has already lost his voice. West Ham’s head coach arrived on Tuesday, watched his side fight back from 3-0 down to draw with Cardiff on Wednesday and was struggling to make himself heard when he met the media on Thursday afternoon.

“It’s like in the summer holidays,” Parker said. “You put the flip-flops on for five weeks, then you come back home and you get your shoes on. You’re in a minute, you’ve got a blister on the back of your heel. It’s the same with a throat. I’ve not shouted for a little while. All of a sudden there’s shouting and it’s a bit croaky.”

Parker is back in the thick of it. Out of work after leaving Burnley in the wake of relegation from the Premier League last April, he cut short his break from management when West Ham parted company with Nuno Espírito Santo. Nuno was sacked early on Tuesday and replaced by Parker, who is intent on leading West Ham out of the Championship at the first time of asking.

It will not be easy. West Ham occupy the final playoff spot after three games without a win and displayed their inconsistencies against Cardiff. They made another slow start, conceding three during the first half, but roared back after a triple half-time change from Parker. Jarrod Bowen was inspired. But Parker needs complete performances if West Ham are to win automatic promotion.

“The Championship’s a tough league,” he said. “It doesn’t matter what name you have on a bit of paper. You have to have a level of humility of what this league needs. That’s a challenge when you come out of the Premier League.”

Parker argued that talent was not enough. Burnley were stingy when they won promotion. Parker has to sort out West Ham’s defence. “Of course we want to play a certain brand,” the 46-year-old said. “But I think it’s just a non-negotiable in terms of a committed team.”

Connections need to be rebuilt with disillusioned supporters. Parker was an all-action midfielder who loved his four years at West Ham as a player. He has added Mark Noble to his backroom staff. Noble has held the role of West Ham’s sporting director since retiring in 2022 but Parker confirmed the former club captain would have a role as an assistant coach. “He’s going to be coaching with me and be that sounding board,” Parker said.

View image in fullscreen Jarrod Bowen was inspired during West Ham’s comeback to earn a 3-3 draw at Cardiff. Photograph: David Davies/PA

Noble will be able to get Parker up to speed on his squad. West Ham need improvement at the back, better balance in midfield and more bite up front. Nils Koppen, the director of recruitment, could be busy in January. Parker wants to give everyone a clean slate, though. Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Álvarez will have opportunities. Even Maxwel Cornet travelled with the squad to Cardiff.

Parker did not focus during negotiations with Karim Virani, West Ham’s interim CEO, and Daniel Kretinsky, the club’s largest shareholder, on whether funds would be available for signings. One step at a time.

West Ham are in transition. David Sullivan still owns a 40% stake but is no longer on the board. Kretinsky’s power has grown, although the Czech billionaire is yet to say much in public. Parker has heard more from Kretinsky than most people.

“I found a man that was hugely passionate,” Parker said. “I instantly felt that, along with Karim, along with Nils. These were three people who know where they want the club to go.”

The target is a return to the top flight. Parker has won promotion with Bournemouth, Burnley and Fulham but his record at keeping teams up is less impressive. He has been dismissed a little unfairly as nothing more than a promotion specialist.

“In a short space of a coaching career I’ve had some huge success,” Parker said. “I’ve had some blips in terms of two full seasons in the Premier League. All I know is that I’m fully committed.”

That mindset convinced Kretinsky, Virani and Koppen to pick Parker. They wanted his knowledge of the club and record at this level.

West Ham are eighth before visiting Blackburn Rovers on Saturday. They are taking 7,000 fans to Ewood Park and Parker knows there can be no more complacency.

Sports.title: Fifa wants talks over restricting women’s Olympic football to under-23s
Sports.content:
Fifa wants talks with the International Olympic Committee over restricting the Olympic women’s football tournament to under-23s owing to concerns over fixture congestion and the workload of senior players.

The eligibility criteria for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles has been set, with qualification tournaments having begun in some regions, so no change can be made until Brisbane 2032 at the earliest, but sources at both organisations have said that they are open to dialogue.

Although no formal proposal has been made, Fifa is understood to be interested in examining the matter in talks with the IOC and other key stakeholders, such as the players and leading member associations whose national sides routinely qualify for the Games.

A move to bring in age restrictions would dramatically alter the nature of the event and require careful analysis, consultation and consideration through Fifa and IOC processes.

Such a change would be controversial and could provoke a backlash from leading international players because the Olympics has long been regarded as one of the highlights of the women’s calendar, with Emma Hayes’s United States team securing gold in Paris two years ago. The Olympic title has been contested eight times and the US have won five.

Women’s football also has a major commercial appeal for the IOC, particularly in markets such as the US, Europe and Australia, so it may resist Fifa’s overtures.

Women’s football was introduced to the Olympics at Atlanta in 1996, and as an amateur sport at that time never had eligibility requirements, in contrast to the men’s game.

After admitting football to the Olympic programme in 1908 the IOC did not permit professionals to take part until 1984 owing to Fifa’s insistence on maintaining the primacy of the World Cup, as well as the demands on players from a congested calendar. Under pressure from Fifa the IOC introduced an under-23 age restriction in 1992, although three overage players have also been allowed in each squad since 1996.

The huge growth and professionalisation of the women’s game over the past decade has created increased fixture congestion, with the 2028 calendar the most bloated yet.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Fifa is to a large extent culpable for this because the world governing body has chosen to launch the Women’s Club World Cup in an Olympic year, with the US to stage the 16-team competition between 5 and 30 January, six months before the Games.

The Women’s Club World Cup will cause major disruption to the European club season, with Arsenal and Chelsea or Manchester City likely to be absent from domestic competition for up to a month if they reach the latter stages, missing four Women’s Super League matches and the FA Cup fourth round. The importance of the sport to the IOC is shown by the fact that the women’s football tournament will be bigger than the men’s for the first time in LA, featuring 16 teams to 12, in a reversal of the numbers at Paris 2024.

Fifa and the IOC declined to comment.

Sports.title: Japan FA’s Kozo Tashima to stand against Infantino for Fifa presidency
Sports.content:
The Japan Football Association’s honorary president, Kozo Tashima, has announced his intention to stand against Gianni Infantino in March’s Fifa presidential election.

Tashima is the second challenger to declare in advance of the 18 November deadline after the former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega, although it remains unclear whether Vega has the backing of five of Fifa’s 211 member associations, which is required to take a place on the ballot in Rabat.

The widely respected Tashima will have no problem in securing the nominations and is understood to have acted with the blessing of Uefa, which has led the opposition to Infantino after his failed attempt to sell off a 20% stake in Fifa’s commercial rights this summer. The former Japan international has many allies in Europe and had talks with Uefa officials at last month’s Asian Football Confederation (AFC) congress in Tokyo.

“I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the Japan Football Association,” Tashima told the Japanese newspaper Sports Nippon. “It’s not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. What Fifa needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order ‌to make this appeal to the world.”

The declaration is an intriguing development after the AFC congress concluded with its president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, publicly endorsing Infantino in a major U-turn, having previously sided with Uefa and Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation – in attempting to depose him.

Tashima could split the AFC vote and is certain to pick up votes from Europe and Concacaf, although other candidates could emerge.

Quick Guide How do I 

Uefa has spent months attempting to find a candidate to stand against Infantino, but may have concluded that a non-European challenger will fare better owing to widespread resentment about its perceived dominance of the sport.

Infantino has the backing of several leading countries in the AFC, such as Qatar and Saudi Arabia, and of Africa and South America, so is expected to canter towards the 106 votes required to be re-elected for a fourth term.

Sports.title: Referee hands out record 53 red cards after chaos at under-20s game in Brazil
Sports.content:
An under-20s match in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais descended into chaos, with the referee handing out a record 53 red cards after a brawl.

The incident took place during the first leg of a state ⁠championship semi-final match between ⁠Uberlandia and ​Mamore. In his report the referee, Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto, said the trouble began early in the second half, ⁠when a number of Uberlandia officials invaded the field after one of their players was sent off.

The match was halted for 40 ⁠minutes and eventually restarted, with Mamore going on to score in the ninth minute of ​stoppage time to take a 3-1 lead.

According ‌to reports in Brazilian ‌media, the Mamore player Davi taunted Uberlandia players during the goal celebrations, which sparked a brawl and led to a deluge of red cards.

A total of 43 players and eight members of the coaching staff were sent off, and two Uberlandia board members were also dismissed.

“In the 54th minute of the second half, a generalised brawl broke out, making it impossible to show the red cards and ‌to carry out the match-closing protocol,” Drosghic Modesto wrote in his report. “Therefore, owing to all the turmoil and the lack of security, I declared ​the match ended.“

Drosghic Modesto added that a police report had been filed over threats made against him and that Mamore’s team had vandalised the dressing room after the match.

The previous Guinness world record for the most red cards shown in a match was 36, which occurred in ⁠February 2011 during a fifth-division match in Argentina between Atlético Claypole and ​Victoriano Arenas.

On Wednesday, Uberlandia ​said it would be forfeiting the ​second leg of the semi-final in a “gesture of fair play” because Mamore ​did not have ‌enough eligible players ​to field a team. The ​forfeit means Mamore qualify for the final.

Uberlandia said: “The club has also not remained silent: the appropriate disciplinary measures regarding those involved have already been taken internally, because athletic development is, above all, a matter of personal development.”

Sports.title: 'Clicky Ponting' cricket cheat slapped with a two-year ban after scandal that went viral - as his village team are booted out of their league and handed huge points deduction
Sports.content:
The cheating club cricketer dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' has been given a two-year ban from the sport following an England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) investigation. In July, footage of Brian Devine, an amateur player for Saltburn's 2nd team, went viral around the world after he was caught deceiving umpires by clicking his fingers as the ball passed the bat to imitate an edge and claim wickets for his team. He was subsequently given the tongue-in-cheek nickname 'Clicky Ponting' – a play on former Australian captain Ricky Ponting – and the scandal caused amusement and outrage in equal measure. Devine has now been banned for two years from involvement in cricket in any form, be that playing, coaching or even scoring, according to Teesside Live. His team on the coast of the north-east of England have also suffered – punished with relegation to the third division where they will start the 2027 season with a 60-point deduction in addition to a £300 fine. A statement from Saltburn CC read: 'The club fully participated in the disciplinary proceedings and accept the decision of the appeal following the original decision from the League. We are now focussing on preparations for the 2027 season. Brian Devine - dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' - has been banned from cricket until September, 2028 'The punishments come after a thorough process which included player interviews, written statements and a detailed review of the video footage. The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League have emailed every club in their system to acknowledge the strain the scandal had caused.' Devine, 38, has played for years at Saltburn Cricket Club and is well known on the cricket scene in North Yorkshire. The father-of-one, from Guisborough, Cleveland, works as a company secretary at Northallerton Auctions, which specialises in auctions for livestock and farm machinery and suddenly became the centre of a story that captured global attention. His outrageous cheating racked up millions of views online and the story came to light after a match against Norton Cricket Club. Footage showed Norton batsman Noman Shabir play at and completely miss his first delivery which had pitched outside the off stump. As the ball passed Shabir the fielder standing at first slip, Devine, clicked his fingers. This imitated the sound of the ball nicking the edge of Shabir's bat and when the wicketkeeper took the catch, the umpire raised his finger to give Shabir out. The game happened to have been live-streamed online and a recording was preserved on the ECB's 'Play Cricket' website.

Your browser does not support iframes.

The Saltburn player was seen on camera clicking his fingers each time the ball neared the bat A Durham-based amateur cricketer named Ben Mummery, who had been tipped off about the series of events, posted footage to X, where he dubbed it 'about the worst case of cheating I have ever seen in cricket'. It racked up millions of views and put Saltburn under international scrutiny from cricket fans across the globe. Viewers turned up dozens of similar incidents from the archives, suggesting that Saltburn (which, ironically, calls itself a 'friendly, sociable and inclusive cricket club') had been employing the cynical scam for more than a season. In almost every one of the clips that emerged, Devine is the fielder standing at first slip. Piers Morgan dubbed the club's behaviour 'outrageous cheating' and a 'shameful scam'. The statistics also outlined the scale of the breathtaking deception. In the 13 matches that Devine played for Saltburn last season, wicketkeepers took an astonishing 39 catches. In the seven that he didn't play, they managed just five. In one match against Shildon Railway on July 18, no fewer than eight catches were claimed by wicketkeeper Josh Bowes. To put that number in perspective, the record for wicketkeeper catches taken in a single men's Test innings, over a period spanning 2,600 matches and 150 years, is a mere seven. Saltburn-by-the-Sea's historic cricket ground, with its white picket fence and neatly mown outfield. Its team have now been booted out the league Devine was suspended by the club when the cheating was unearthed online and also faced the ignominy of being ditched by his official sponsor, a local Indian restaurant named Spices which he patronises regularly. Back in July when the scandal broke, it was left to Georgina Vaughn, the mother of Devine's partner Clare, to defend his honour. She told Guy Adams, Daily Mail Senior Feature Writer: 'It was only a little village cricket match and now it's become this thing that's all over the news and social media. It has got totally out of hand and there is nothing any of us want to say.' Asked whether Devine was a man of integrity, she replied: 'He certainly is.' The ECB's investigation has found otherwise and Devine will not be able to return to the sport until September 2028.

Sports.title: Pressure mounts on under-fire Regis Le Bris as Sunderland lose again, Bournemouth's super-subs preserve their flawless start, Pierre Sage is handed a Crystal Palace lifeline after late equaliser, while Brighton win
Sports.content:
Sunderland's unbeaten start to their first European campaign in 53 years was brought to an abrupt end by Dinamo Zagreb to pile more pressure on Regis Le Bris ahead of Chelsea's visit to Wearside. The Croatian side won 2-0 to heap more misery on Le Bris and his team at the Stadium of Light following a dismal start to the season in which his team has won just one Premier League fixture. There were Bonfire Night fireworks across Wearside, and before the game at the Stadium of Light, but not enough on the pitch from Sunderland, who only came to life after the break. Europa League football has been an antidote to domestic doom and gloom for Sunderland fans, with the club having made a bright start to its first European campaign in 53 years by winning two and drawing one of their first three group phase fixtures. But it was Dinamo who would light up the first half with two moments of quality from Luke Stojkovic and Dion Beljo. Le Bris had labelled the season as 'probably the most demanding challenge Sunderland has faced in its history' before the game, which followed a 3-1 defeat by newly-promoted Coventry City. The 3-1 loss left the Carabao Cup quarter-finalists rooted to the bottom of the Premier League with just five points from nine games, and Le Bris under scrutiny ahead of a challenging run of fixtures. Roger Le Bris is under increasing pressure at Sunderland after seeing his side lose once again Granit Xhaka cuts a forlorn figure as Sunderland's unbeaten Europa League start ends Le Bris, mindful of Sunday's Premier League game against fourth-placed Chelsea, made six changes against the Croatian champions, leaving top scorer Brian Brobbey on the bench along with influential midfielder Enzo Le Fee. Le Bris also labelled the club's domestic struggles this term as 'growing pains', and Sunderland are not the first promoted club to suffer second-season syndrome. The problem for them is that they also have to contend with a lot more games due to their success last season. The Black Cats found Dinamo, who parted company with domestic double-winning manager Mario Kovacevic following a shock defeat by newly-promoted Rudes on Saturday, hard to break down in the first 15 minutes, and when Chris Rigg did get in behind after being found by captain Granit Xhaka, Jules Ahoka could not get enough power on his header. Dinamo's Stojkovic, however, could not have hit his effort at the other end of the pitch any better. With Wilson Isidor waiting to come back on the pitch following treatment, the visitors, backed by 1,500 noisy fans, won a corner. Xhaka headed it away from goal, but only as far as Stojkovic, who chested the ball down and superbly volleyed it past Robin Roefs to put Dinamo ahead. Thomas Meunier then clipped the woodwork with a cross aimed for the head of Isidor before things got even worse for the home side. Kevin Danso's weak clearance found Stojkovic, who clipped the ball to Beljo, who then dinked it over Roefs to put his team in control at the break. Le Fee was one of four players sent on by Le Bris for the second half, and a goal from Isidor - he headed Xhaka's free-kick home - was ruled out for offside a minute after the restart. Sunderland, at least, were playing with some much-needed urgency following a lacklustre first 45 minutes, and Danso hit the crossbar during a spell of pressure from Le Bris's side. Sunderland fans vented their frustration, both at their team and referee Andrea Colombo, as the second half wore on. Luka Stojkovic scored Dinamo Zagreb's opener in their 2-0 win with this sublime strike But Sunderland, for all their second-half possession, rarely tested goalkeeper Dominik Kotarski, Dinamo saw the game out to condemn Sunderland to only their second defeat in European competition, the last having come against Sporting Lisbon in the 1973-74 season. Le Bris must now quickly pick up his side ahead of the visit of Chelsea. Progression in Europe is important for the club, and Sunderland should still avoid elimination when the Europa League's group phase ends, but nowhere near as important as preserving its Premier League status. Sparta Prague 1-3 Bournemouth - Cherries come from behind to maintain 100 per cent start in Europa League By Luke Augustus Forget the icing on the cake, the Cherries joint-top, second on goal difference, of the Europa League after their come-from-behind 3-1 win at Sparta Prague. After winning just one of their opening eight matches in all competitions, Bournemouth have now won seven on the bounce thanks to second-half goals from Tyler Adams, Evanilson and Rayan. All three came on as second-half substitutes to underline the quality that Marco Rose has at his disposal. 'You can't get too comfortable. You have to continue to hold that standard,' reflected Adams post-match. 'That winning mentality becomes continuous, especially when you're playing every three days.' Rose, who made eight changes to his XI, will be delighted with his side's fight but will also thank Sparta centre-back Tobias Guddal who inexplicably got himself sent off in the first half for two avoidable yellow cards. Prior to Guddal's red card, Sparta were in the ascendancy and should have taken the lead when striker Jonatan Braut Brunes, Erling Haaland's cousin, inexplicably put wide a tap-in in the opening two minutes. That was the biggest chance in the match until Bournemouth were awarded a penalty midway through the first half. Former Liverpool defender Ki-Jana Hoever, who is on loan from Wolves, was booked for a handball in the box. Lewis Cook's stutter run-up fooled Jakub Surovcik but saw his low effort hit the inside of the left-hand post before rolling out of play. Evanilson was on the scoresheet as Bournemouth came from behind to win at Sparta Prague Fellow substitute Tyler Adams (second left) started the visitors' 3-1 comeback with this finish Rayan celebrates after adding a third for Bournemouth to complete their memorable victory If Cook was unlucky, there was no element of luck to Sparta breaking the deadlock. Counter-attacking from a Cherries' corner, Surovcik threw the ball out to Ebrima Singhateh inside his own half. The impressive winger shrugged off Cook before beginning his brilliant run, which included slaloming in between Bournemouth players, and scoring. It was a goal befitting of the Champions League, let alone the Europa League. Sparta's joy was short-lived as Guddal, who had already been booked for a foul on Ben Gannon-Doak, then inexplicably brought down Alvaro Rodriguez. Rose turned to his bench at half-time and all of his changes worked as they pressed Sparta into mistakes. Adams was the beneficiary for their first goal as he scored with a low right-footed shot from outside the box 12 minutes after coming on. With 10 minutes remaining Evanilson put the visitors ahead with a sublime curled effort into the far corner with no backlift. 'He's on fire right now, but you see him do it every day in training,' Adams purred about his team-mate. For him to do it in a game is no surprise. He has so much quality. 'Whenever he gets in and around the box, we're confident he's going to find the back of the net.' Ebrima Singhateh scored the goal of the game to give Sparta the lead after a stunning solo run Before Singhateh's stunner, Lewis Cook saw his penalty hit the inside of the post and go out Evanilson then turned provider, via a neat one-two, to see Rayan score from distance. The result means it's four out of four in the Europa League for the European debutants. With Celta Vigo away next after the international break, don't be surprised if it's five out of five. Crystal Palace 1-1 Hoffenheim - Under-fire Eagles boss Pierre Sage given a let-off thanks to Daichi Kamada By Will Pickworth at Selhurst Park As the fourth official signalled three minutes of added time, Pierre Sage may have been cursing his luck on the Selhurst Park touchline. Although he has been hampered by the absences of Jean-Philippe Mateta, Ismaila Sarr and Dean Henderson at points this season, plus a transfer strategy that has left him shorn of experience and quality in key areas, the Frenchman was approaching a record of eight defeats in 13 league and European games. Two seasons ago, Crystal Palace's hierarchy kept faith with Oliver Glasner when his side won one of their first 13 matches - a record that preceded the greatest 18 months in the club's history - but Sage was running out of time to prove he deserved a similar demonstration of trust. Enter Daichi Kamada, Palace's best player here, as he finished calmly through the legs of Hoffenheim goalkeeper Oliver Baumann to rescue a valuable point for his side. But this was a let-off for Sage on a night that had felt like it could precede the final days of his tenure, and he must now summon an improved display against Liverpool this weekend. 'Conceding early in the game was difficult because we had to push to come back,' Sage said post-match. 'But we scored at the end, and the players deserved it because they didn't give up.' Daichi Kamara earned Crystal Palace a point in second-half stoppage-time against Hoffenheim Hoffenheim took the lead in the 1-1 encounter when Alexander Prass (second right) scored Palace's equaliser came when down to 10 men after Adam Wharton's (centre) earlier dismissal There was nothing to sum up Palace's predicament quite like Alexander Prass' early opener. Having started well - with Kamada having a goal ruled out for offside - Quinten Timber saw a penalty appeal waved away before the out-of-form Adam Wharton was dispossessed. The German side broke forward at electric speed and Prass' effort squirmed through Henderson. It was an all too familiar story as Palace's defence - weakened by Sage's decision to leave Axel Disasi out of his squad in what he later labelled 'an internal decision' - again looked ill-equipped for the challenge in hand. 'Offensively we did better than our two previous games, but we have to continue to improve defensively because we gave too much space to them,' Sage added. 'When we defend too much, we have no chance to exist in the game, and when we try to attack a little bit, we are quickly open. You don't exist in the game when you don't attack. For this team the best way to defend is to keep the ball with efficiency.' The hosts were careless on the ball though, doing little to improve the subdued atmosphere at Selhurst Park, and although Yeremy Pino and Kamada spurned good chances, Hoffenheim appeared to have closed out the game. Palace's late equaliser eases the pressure on under-fire boss Pierre Sage for now Palace's frustration was demonstrated by four yellow cards in seven minutes, before Wharton received a second shortly after to compound their misery. The home faithful threatened to turn restless and it looked like the night would end in disappointment, until Kamada's strike gave Sage a lifeline. Getafe 0-1 Brighton - Seagulls are beginning to soar across the continent as Pascal Gross inspires victory By James Sharpe Trust Pascal Gross to seize the moment. For a little over an hour, Brighton toiled and laboured in pursuit of the goal that would ignite their European dreams. The Seagulls have made light work of the Premier League, these vanquishers of Arsenal and Manchester City and now are starting to stretch their dominance across the continent. Gnarly minnows Getafe love to make life deeply unpleasant for their opponents and Brighton, for all their energy and endeavour, looked destined to be unable to find the answers. Yet there he was, this 35-year-old starting a remarkable 16th straight game of the season when it mattered. There was Gross, afforded too much space on the left, allowed to spot the run of Joao Costinha towards the back post. Naturally, the German landed his raking cross right on Costinha's head. The wing-back nodded it across goal for Malick Yalcouye to send a header of his own into the top corner to win it and send Brighton, who are yet to concede in the competition, into the Conference League play-off places and their fans dreaming of European glory. 'The fans should dream and, hopefully at one point, maybe we fulfil their dream,' said Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler. Malick Yalcouye (centre) scored the winner as Brighton won 1-0 at Getafe in the Europa Conference League 'We focus on work and we focus on the things we can control. We didn't play our best game. We had a few moments where we were lazy with the easy things. We didn't do the simple things on the highest level. But we kept a clean sheet, scored in the right moment and I think we deserve to win this game.' Getafe, this modest club from the outskirts of Madrid, have long lived in the shadow of their monumental neighbours Real and Atletico but have also earned a famous reputation for a good old-fashioned giant killing. They once beat Barcelona 4-0 here to overturn a three-goal deficit to reach the Copa del Rey final and then did them again in the league the following season. They went up the road to the Bernabeu in March and came away with three points. Brighton, meanwhile, have made such a habit of turning over the bigger boys that, for the Seagulls, it's stopped becoming that extraordinary. They mix so frequently among the giants these days that it's often easy to see the Seagulls as ones themselves. Getafe certainly would. What was always going to be fascinating was the clash of styles. Brighton, with their relentless press and free-flowing football under Fabian Hurzeler, against a physical Getafe side that boasts the lowest possession and pass success rate in La Liga. There's a reason their players have already been shown six red cards They certainly made it awkward for Brighton at times here. Bart Verbruggen was twice called upon to deny Getafe striker Ivan Azon in the first half – initially after some chaos inside the Brighton box and secondly after a desperately poor back pass from Olivier Boscagli on the stroke of the break. Unlike in their Premier League exploits, Hurzeler's side struggled to find that bit of quality when it mattered. Georginio Rutter, in his first start since August, fizzed a cross to the back post but it eluded Yasin Ayari, the hero of the Eithad, and then fired a shot of his own wide. Heaven only knows how the ball didn't end up in the net when Jaouen Hadjam, Brighton's brightest spark, raced through on goal but couldn't beat the keeper or the post and Yalcouye's rebound couldn't find the gaping goalmouth. Hadjam flicked the top of the crossbar with another effort in the second half before substitute Luka Vuskovic blazed another over. Thankfully, as so often is the case, Gross was there to make it count.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer's England lifeline: Three Lions ask Chelsea about star's fitness in clear sign Thomas Tuchel is considering calling him up after warning over last squad withdrawal
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer's England lifeline: Three Lions ask Chelsea about star's fitness in clear sign Thomas Tuchel is considering calling him up after warning over last squad withdrawal

England have privately asked Chelsea for the latest on Cole Palmer ahead of Thomas Tuchel revealing his squad for the Nations League clashes with Croatia and Spain.

Palmer is under consideration for another call-up, having withdrawn from duty during the last international break with a minor muscular injury.

Tuchel responded by appearing to question his desire to represent his country, warning he 'misses way too many camps' as the 24-year-old skipped all four England fixtures in September and October.

Palmer had played a full 90 for Chelsea away at Bournemouth before that break, which he then used to fly abroad to the Caribbean with his girlfriend, Olivia Holder, after withdrawing from England duty. He was accompanied by a personal rehab coach on that trip, and was provided with an injury-specific training and recovery plan by his club.

Palmer started in Chelsea's first fixture when the Premier League returned at home to Brentford with Blues boss Xabi Alonso insisting they were right to take care of their star player themselves.

Chelsea star Cole Palmer is under consideration for England UEFA Nations League call-up

He withdrew from the last squad, leaving boss Thomas Tuchel questioning his commitment

Palmer, who was injured, went to the Caribbean with girlfriend Olivia Holder on the last international break

It has been described as standard procedure for England to make medical checks on players with clubs. While it does not guarantee a call-up, it indicates how Tuchel has been weighing up offering Palmer another chance as he names his next squad on Friday morning.

Palmer was not the only player to withdraw from England duty in the last break, with Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento among other dropouts.

Yet Palmer's issue was a contentious topic after it represented a chance for him to return to England's thinking following his 2026 World Cup omission. His representative did not answer when asked whether he would happily accept another call-up after Tuchel's previous comments.

Palmer has played an important role for Chelsea early in this season with three goals and three assists in the Premier League.

He scored a penalty in their last win over Manchester United, which took him to 50 goals in 105 games in the top flight for the Blues. He has started every league game under Alonso this term with Sunderland at the Stadium of Light this Sunday.

Sports.title: Tennis billionaire heiress Jessica Pegula is caught on hot mic saying 19-year-old rival Mirra Andreeva is a 'diva who needs to be humbled'
Sports.content:
Billionaire tennis heiress Jessica Pegula has been caught red-handed gossiping about her 19-year-old rival Mirra Andreeva.

The American star, 32, was caught calling Andreeva a 'diva' who 'needs to be humbled' by a microphone that she was unaware of during training.

She also said she had 'lost respect' for legendary Spanish player Conchita Martínez, who now coaches Andreeva, this year's French Open champion.

Andreeva has gained a reputation for her fiery temperament – at Wimbledon this year she smashed her rackets, snapped at the umpire and her team, said 'I quit,' and left the court in tears after losing to Barbora Krejcikova in the second round.

Pegula, daughter of £8.9billion oil and gas tycoon Terry Pegula, was recorded by a hot mic while training for WTA Finals in Indian Wells.

'Conchita has always been very nice to me, but I've lost a little bit of respect for her,' she began.

Jessica Pegula (left) was caught on a hot mic saying Mirra Andreeva is a 'diva' who 'needs to be humbled'

Andreeva, 19, is known for her explosive outbursts on court, including smashing her rackets

Pegula is the heiress in a billionaire family but has worked hard to reach her position (Instagram: @jpegula)

'I think she's a nice girl, she's just a diva. She needs to be humbled. You have to put her in her place.

'Do it, stand up to her. If I was a coach, and my girl just played four great games, and you're up 4-0, and you're mad at me throwing balls at me, first of all, that's so disrespectful. You're up 4-0, like shut the f*** up.

'But she can't. Conchita pokes her and eggs on her behaviour. She has a perfect serve, she's smart, she anticipates well.

'If she had Coco's mentality, she's better, serve, everything, all around. Mentally she's just...'

Pegula also swirled her finger close to her temple, appearing to indicate that she thought Andreeva was crazy.

The pair are yet to face each other in competitive action, but they could in this tournament. While Andreeva won the French Open this year, Pegula is still waiting to win a Grand Slam – she reached the final of the US Open in 2024.

Pegula has come under fire for her 'diva' comments, particularly because of her high-ranking background.

Her father grew rich through oil and gas – he founded East Resources to explore those markets in 1983 with a loan of $7,500 (£5,565) before selling most of its assets in 2010 for nearly $5billion (£3.710billion).

Pegula, left, with her family after her parents Terry and Kim bought the Buffalo Bills in 2014

Andreeva regularly lets the umpire, her team, and the crowd know about her frustrations

Together with his wife, Kim, Pegula now invests in sports teams. They own the NHL's Buffalo Sabres and in 2014 they beat groups spearheaded by Donald Trump and Bon Jovi to buy the NFL's Buffalo Bills for $1.4bn (£1.038bn).

But Pegula told Daily Mail Sport a couple of summers ago: 'It's funny when people assume that I fly private everywhere, or that I have had a chauffeur driving me around since I was five… I grew up pretty normal, and a lot of that [her family's wealth] didn't happen to me until I was already older and playing.

'My goal since I was six or seven was to be No 1 in the world… I was just a normal kid growing up in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, taking lessons after school.'

That hasn't shielded Pegula, 32, from allegations that, to win a Grand Slam, she 'needs [a] dynamic that family billions can't buy'.

It is fair for her to indicate that Andreeva has an explosive character on court. The Wimbledon incident was far from the first.

At the French Open last year, she imploded on her way to defeat against world No361 Lois Boisson and hit a ball into the crowd, which brought on boos and a warning.

At Indian Wells in March this year, she threw and smashed her racket after losing against Katerina Siniakova, before exchanging heated words with members of the crowd.

'I feel like it’s not the best way to handle yourself, but once in a while it really helps to get mad at yourself and get it done,' she has said.

She also says she should try and learn from Serena Williams: 'I think the one person that was handling losses very well was Serena Williams, like I've never heard or seen her upset.

'Even I remember, she was losing finals on the Slams, and she would always smile and be happy for her opponent that she won the match and she got the trophy. So maybe it's something that I can also try to learn, and we'll see how that's gonna go. Yeah, we'll see.'

Sports.title: Liam Rosenior says Chelsea sacking had 'nothing to do with football' as he raises questions about 'tolerance' in England in first revelations about being axed just three months into the job
Sports.content:
Liam Rosenior says Chelsea sacking had 'nothing to do with football' as he raises questions about 'tolerance' in England in first revelations about being axed just three months into the job

Liam Rosenior has claimed he was treated unfairly during his doomed 106 days in charge of Chelsea, and that the way it ended in disaster had ‘nothing to do with football’.

Rosenior was relieved of his duties after losing five consecutive games without scoring. The fifth defeat in that run – a 3-0 loss at Brighton in which Chelsea did not even muster a shot on target – saw the players accused of downing tools to get rid of their head coach. He lasted 106 days in total.

However, Rosenior, now manager of Paris FC, who are fourth in France’s Ligue 1, has claimed his Stamford Bridge sacking was 'nothing to do with football' in a cryptic comment about 'tolerance' in English football.

The 42-year-old Englishman took aim at ‘the media’ in particular as he said in an interview with So Foot: ‘It was the best experience of my life, and the hardest, too. It was fantastic, even though it only lasted four months. I don’t want to go into details now. I’ll talk about it one day, when the time is right. But in a country where tolerance is an important value, what happened there has nothing to do with football.’

Pressed to explain, Rosenior continued: ‘I know, I answered without answering it. Actually, the moment that worried me the most was at the beginning, when we went through that five-game winning streak.

Liam Rosenior was seen passing a note to Alejandro Garnacho with Chelsea 8-2 down on aggregate against PSG - and the reaction to it clearly still rankles with him

Then-Chelsea manager Rosenior was compared to The Office star David Brent online

‘Any club would have been happy with such a run, but not Chelsea. You get good results and you’re in the spotlight. Then, there was a kind of snowball effect in the media.

‘They made fun of those instructions I gave (Alejandro) Garnacho on a scrap of paper when we were down to 10 men against PSG (during the second leg in March as they lost 8-2 on aggregate).

'The clothes I wore became a joke, the way I spoke, too. I’m not a joke! You’re the first people I’m talking to about this, and probably the last for a long time, but one day, I’ll tell you what really happened.’

It is unclear whether by ‘the media’, Rosenior meant those reporters who covered the club or social media, where he was routinely mocked and referred to as ‘LinkedIn Liam’.

Those within the actual Chelsea pack who attended Rosenior’s press conferences believe he was treated kindly despite the Blues boss not helping himself at times.

For example, his decision to suddenly drop Robert Sanchez for Filip Jorgensen backfired, especially in their Champions League last-16 first-leg loss away at PSG. When Jorgensen was then injured, Sanchez returned to the starting line-up with his confidence having been dented.

Rosenior also created a stir when he argued with a member of Arsenal’s support staff for encroaching in Chelsea’s half during their warm-up before the second leg of their Carabao Cup semi-final. He accused his opponents of breaking the ‘etiquettes in football’ afterwards.

After his players huddled around the referee Paul Tierney in the centre circle before a Premier League loss to Newcastle, Rosenior defended their pre-match routine. He described it as being designed to ‘respect the ball’ – words which were also ridiculed on social media, even if that idea did originate from Willie Isa, Chelsea’s hire from rugby league.

The former Strasbourg manager is now enjoying life back in France as manager of Paris FC

Rosenior added in his interview that he was never accepted in the Premier League, saying: ‘In England, there’s this preconceived notion of what a Premier League coach should be, how he should behave. You have to conform to that standard. People who know me know that I’m someone who tries to be sincere and authentic.

‘But I don’t have control over how the media describes me or talks about me. What I’ve understood now, and this is important for all coaches worldwide, is that social media, or the media in general, can dictate public opinion about the quality of a player or a coach.

‘This isn’t new, of course, but the biggest lesson from my time at Chelsea is knowing that they are also capable of constructing the entire narrative around a club’s trajectory.’

Sports.title: Aussie cricket star Chris Lynn's secret cocaine ban after drug binge following quarter-final victory
Sports.content:
Aussie cricket star Chris Lynn's secret cocaine ban after drug binge following quarter-final victory

Australian cricket star Chris Lynn served a one-month cocaine ban that has only now become public, after failing a drug test on the day he helped Northamptonshire win England's T20 Blast title.

The 36-year-old admitted to using cocaine over several hours following his side's quarter-final victory in July, with his suspension subsequently reduced after he completed a substance-abuse treatment program.

Lynn served the ban from July 31 to August 30. The sanction emerged publicly on Friday, months after he had completed it and amid reports linking him with a Big Bash League move to the Melbourne Renegades.

The former Australian international provided a urine sample during T20 Blast Finals Day at Edgbaston on July 18.

He scored 39 in the semi-final and four in the final as Northamptonshire claimed the trophy for the third time.

Analysis at a World Anti-Doping Agency-accredited laboratory in France detected benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

Chris Lynn served a one-month cocaine ban that only became public months after his suspension ended

The Australian batter, pictured with partner Karlie, tested positive after helping Northamptonshire win the T20 Blast title on July 18

ynn's proposed three-month suspension was reduced to one month after he completed a substance-abuse treatment program

Lynn subsequently acknowledged taking the drug on July 15 and into the early hours of July 16, several days before the test.

Earlier on July 15, he had retired hurt during Northamptonshire's quarter-final win over Gloucestershire after being struck on the foot by a low full toss from Duan Jansen.

England's Cricket Regulator accepted evidence that Lynn's cocaine use took place out of competition and was unrelated to sporting performance.

After the Blast, Lynn travelled to Sri Lanka for the Lanka Premier League, making one appearance for Galle Gallants before being ruled out with a leg injury on July 29.

Two days later, the regulator notified him of his positive test and imposed a provisional suspension.

Lynn responded on August 20, admitting the cocaine use and supplying evidence about when it had occurred.

The regulator initially pursued two charges under the England and Wales Cricket Board's anti-doping rules.

One was subsequently dropped because the concentration detected in his sample fell below the minimum threshold required for that charge.

The former Australian international served his suspension from July 31 to August 30

Lynn, pictured with footy star Reagan Campbell-Gillard, accepted the sanction after the regulator dropped one of the two original anti-doping charges

The remaining breach carried a proposed three-month suspension. That was reduced to one month after Lynn provided confirmation he had completed a substance-abuse treatment program.

His suspension was deemed completed on August 30, with formal notice of the charges following on September 23. Lynn accepted the sanction.

Cocaine is prohibited in competition under the anti-doping rules and is also classified as a substance of abuse.

The regulator's acceptance that Lynn used it outside competition, without a connection to sporting performance, was central to the penalty imposed.

Lynn has not played professional cricket since his brief stint in Sri Lanka.

His playing future is now back in the spotlight after he reportedly agreed to join the Melbourne Renegades for the upcoming BBL season. The signing has not been officially announced.

One of Australia's most recognisable T20 power hitters, Lynn played four one-day internationals and 18 T20 internationals for his country, with his most recent Australian appearance coming in 2018.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk is spot on: Liverpool's brittle defence leaves them looking like a vulnerable mess - it is unsustainable and MUST be fixed, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk is spot on: Liverpool's brittle defence leaves them looking like a vulnerable mess - it is unsustainable and MUST be fixed, writes LEWIS STEELE

Liverpool's defensive woes are not sustainable, insists skipper Virgil van Dijk who says the team cannot accept losing in the way they did at Fenerbahce.

The Reds lost 3-2 having twice led in Istanbul, with individual errors and lapses in concentration costing them.

Andoni Iraola’s men have now suffered back-to-back defeats after also losing to Arsenal – and they have conceded three goals in each of their last three European games, against LASK, Villarreal and Fenerbahce.

When this statistic was put to Van Dijk, he said: ‘(Our defending) is definitely not sustainable. That’s why it is a very disappointing night, for many reasons but definitely the goals we conceded and the manner we conceded them as well. There is work to do.

‘It is very, very tough. Three set pieces as well. We have been very good at them so far this season but we switched off and were not ready for the first and second balls. Yeah, it is a tough one to take.

‘I mentioned after the last game, we as a group have to go through good moments but also lesser good moments. That will only form a bigger bond, it will be only beneficial.

Liverpool suffered a disappointing 3-2 Champions League loss to Fenerbahce on Wednesday

Captain Virgil van Dijk insisted Liverpool's poor defending is not 'sustainable' after the game

‘No one wants to lose games especially how we did today but it should only help us in the near future. We should not accept losing, especially in the manner we did today.’

Asked if he was angry, the Dutchman said: ‘Yes. But I didn’t show it today because everyone looked disappointed and they have a reason to be, they should be disappointed. We cannot lose in the manner we did today. But we did that and it is down to Fenerbahce as well.’

Analysis: Reds' defence is a mess

By LEWIS STEELE

Van Dijk is right. The defence has been all over the place at times this season – especially in Europe.

Iraola thought he had won the game with a masterstroke triple substitution just after the hour mark when Cody Gakpo assisted Alexander Isak two minutes after the pair joined Florian Wirtz in entering the field.

But in trying to win the game – which is commendable – Iraola left the back door open. It felt ajar all night as Fenerbahce continually had joy down the flanks.

Van Dijk was asked if the deafening atmosphere of the Istanbul crowd played a part and said: ‘It is very difficult for everyone on the pitch because you can’t communicate easily.’

That could be an excuse but these players are world class and cannot put too much blame on the atmosphere.

Jeremy Jacquet has been imperious since joining from Rennes but the Frenchman had his first bad game in a Liverpool shirt, while Van Dijk was not too much better.

Milos Kerkez (above) and Kostas Tsimikas are proving a serious problem at left back

Leaky Liverpool's defensive record November 3: Fenerbahce 3-2 Liverpool October 20: Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal October 14: LASK 3-6 Liverpool September 9: Liverpool 2-1 Atletico Madrid *In the Champions League this season

Alisson, too, has left questions to be asked over his performances of late. After giving the ball away cheaply for Arsenal’s winner on Sunday, he was at fault for Fenerbahce’s decisive goal by dilly-dallying over whether to come for a cross. He should have gobbled it up.

But the real problem is at full back. Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas are not good enough – not now, anyway. That should be first on the priority list in future transfer windows.

Ronald Araujo, rested on the night, was missed.

The approach of ‘you can score, we will score more’ has been used – intentionally or not – in most European games this term. When it comes off, as it did in 6-3 and 4-3 wins over LASK and Villarreal respectively, it is exciting.

When it doesn’t, Liverpool just look a vulnerable mess. Work to do for Iraola ahead of a trip to Selhurst Park and Crystal Palace on Sunday, where Pierre Sage is fighting for his life.

Sports.title: Newcastle star Amar Dedic sparks six-car police swoop after being spotted with a BOW AND ARROWS in Northumberland beauty spot before weapon is seized
Sports.content:
Newcastle United star Amar Dedic was at the centre of a major police operation after he was spotted carrying a bow and arrows at a Northumberland beauty spot – with at least SIX patrol cars involved in the search for the £30million defender.

The Bosnia international sparked alarm when a concerned member of the public reported seeing him and a friend walking with the weapon near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the area in Harlow Hill, with some understood to have been armed response units, before Dedic and his companion were finally intercepted around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate.

Sources have described the dramatic swoop on Dedic's vehicle before officers searched the car and seized a bow and arrows, with the 24-year-old questioned about his activities.

In a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic. It is understood the pair were in the area by chance and stopped to offer assistance.

After speaking to the two men, officers were satisfied there was no threat to the public, with police subsequently stating that the equipment was believed to have been intended for recreational use.

Amar Dedic played in Newcastle's 1-0 defeat by Everton on Monday evening

Dedic was spotted with a crossbow off Military Road, the 61-mile B6318 in Northumberland

However, enquiries remain ongoing into the incident, which happened on Wednesday afternoon. It is understood that Dedic and his friend had fired some arrows while in the countryside, although it remains unclear what they were aiming at. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in the UK.

Dedic joined Newcastle from Benfica during the summer and has impressed at right back despite the club's difficult start to the season.

Daily Mail Sport understands he will not face disciplinary action from Newcastle over the incident, although there is a feeling that the player was naive to believe he could walk around the countryside carrying such weaponry.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson said: 'Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.

'Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows. At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing.'

Dedic is expected to be available for Saturday's Premier League trip to Fulham, where Newcastle will attempt to halt a run of four defeats in five matches across all competitions.

Sports.title: 'Clicky Ponting' banned as his cricket club suffer harsh punishment for cheating scandal
Sports.content:
'Clicky Ponting' banned as his cricket club suffer harsh punishment for cheating scandal

Brian Devine, who became known as "Clicky Ponting" after his cheating in amateur cricket matches went viral, has received a punishment alongside his club Saltburn CC

View 3 Images "Clicky Ponting" cricket cheating scandal

An amateur cricketer who was dubbed "Clicky Ponting" after his cheating went viral around the world has been slapped with a two-year ban.

‌



‌



Brian Devine, who played for Saltburn Cricket Club's 2nd team, found himself at the centre of a sporting scandal over the summer after footage of his behaviour found a wider audience.

‌



Devine was caught red-handed clicking as the ball passed the bat, conning the umpire into giving caught-behind decisions. He was quickly handed the name Clicky Ponting as coverage of the story went national and then international.

‌



As reported by Teeside Live, Devine and his club on the north east coast of England have now been handed punishments by the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) following an investigation.

View 3 Images Brian Devine has been banned for two years for cheating (Image: X)

Devine has been handed a two-year ban from all cricket, which runs until September 29, 2028. It covers playing, coaching umpiring, scoring and managing junior teams.

‌



Meanwhile, Saltburn's 2nd team have been relegated to the third division and will start the 2027 season with a 60-point deduction. They have also been fined £300.

A statement from Saltburn CC read: "The club fully participated in the disciplinary proceedings and accept the decision of the appeal following the original decision from the League. We are now focussing on preparations for the 2027 season."

‌



The punishments come after a thorough process which included player interviews, written statements and a detailed review of the video footage. The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League have emailed every club in their system to acknowledge the strain the scandal had caused.

View 3 Images Saltburn Cricket Club were swept up by the scandal (Image: Ian Forsyth/Getty Images)

‌



Saltburn suspended Devine in the wake of the scandal in July. It made headlines after a video of him clicking to dismiss a batter for Norton went viral on social media.

Saltburn won the match by 159 runs to go 17 points clear at the top of their division. At the time, their statement read: “We are treating this allegation with the utmost seriousness and, as a family-centric Club, we are fully cooperating with the NYSD League's investigation.

Article continues below

“We believe that the club acted decisively as soon as the complaint and investigation were made known to us. The player at the centre of the complaint has been suspended and will not play again for the club this season or in the foreseeable future, pending the outcome of this investigation. Initial discussions have already taken place between club officials and the league.

“This has been a very distressing and stressful experience for all those concerned, and we would ask that this reality is borne in mind and that personal boundaries are respected, as we are an amateur club entirely run by volunteers. We will be making no further comment at this time.”

Sports.title: Jason Wilcox singled out as Man Utd rivals say transfer 'cost £25m too much'
Sports.content:
Jason Wilcox singled out as Man Utd rivals say transfer 'cost £25m too much'

Jason Wilcox has taken huge flack from Manchester United players and supporters with rival Premier League teams now questioning his transfer decisions

View 2 Images The fee agreed between Manchester United and Chelsea for Andrey Santos has been questioned (Image: (Photo by Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Manchester United's summer transfer business continues to be questioned with fresh reports claiming that Andrey Santos should have cost half the £50million agreed with Chelsea. The Brazilian was one of three midfielders to arrive at Old Trafford ahead of the 2026/27 season with Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba also joining.

‌



‌



Fresh off a superb season at Aston Villa, the former costing just £35m looked to be a bargain but he has had a difficult start to life at Old Trafford. Baleba, who signed for the club injured, cost twice that fee which drew criticism, particularly following a mixed last campaign at Brighton.

‌



Santos, meanwhile, had not featured too regularly until the injury suffered by Kobbie Mainoo but he has looked out of place in United's midfield. The 22-year-old joined Chelsea in January 2023 but managed only 47 senior outings before his July move to United.

‌



Considering his potential and the inflated transfer market, the £50m price tag seemed reasonable for United and director of football Jason Wilcox, but it has since emerged that Chelsea viewed it as an excellent piece of business.

‌



According to The Athletic, sources close to the Blues believe he was worth only half the £50million they pocketed for his departure.

Their assessment suggests that for United, the spending reflected a market where prices had soared, and the acquisitions were crucial for bolstering squad depth. There's also a case to be made that Santos and Baleba are young enough to continue their development.

‌



Nevertheless, one United source involved in recruitment said: “Jason is cool-headed, very smart and pays close attention to details.”

Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes were among other Premier League midfielders linked with United who ended up elsewhere. The latter pair both moved to Tottenham for a combined £185m, while Anderson's switch from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City set a new transfer record for an English player at £116m — albeit until Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester United duo Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba are viewed as signings for the future

United lacked the financial muscle to splash such sums on a single player, with a return to the Champions League likely influencing the decision to prioritise quantity over quality.

‌



Kobbie Mainoo has remained as Carrick's go-to choice in the middle of the park and is expected to partner Santos against Aston Villa on Sunday. It's already evident that pairing him with Tielemans in midfield isn't effective, while Baleba looks set to be sidelined through injury.

Speaking on the latter after he was helped off earlier this week, Carrick said: "I haven't got any more news on Carlos at this stage, but it's his hamstring. We'll have to assess what that looks like, but initially, it doesn't look great."

‌



Carrick retains the option of deploying Tielemans in a more advanced midfield position to compensate for his limitations in terms of pace and mobility when operating deeper. This tactical shift has resulted in Bruno Fernandes being pushed out wide to the right before ultimately being left out of the starting XI completely.

Fernandes has since been restored to the first team for recent fixtures against Chelsea and Roma, netting his first goal since early September in the latter encounter. He also delivered the cross that set up Matheus Cunha's first goal, while Shea Lacey provided the assist for his match-winner.

Article continues below

After an impressive substitute appearance, there are growing demands for the young United talent to be handed a starting berth ahead of Amad, who has registered just one assist since his comeback from injury last month.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta decision to force Arsenal transfer exit as player's father speaks his mind
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta decision to force Arsenal transfer exit as player's father speaks his mind

Mikel Merino has played a limited role for Arsenal this season, starting just once in the Premier League

View 2 Images Mikel Merino has only started once in the Premier League so far this season

Mikel Merino's limited game time under Mikel Arteta could prompt an Arsenal exit, with his midfielder's father speaking about a potential return to Spain. The Spaniard regularly makes his presence felt, whether starting or coming off the bench, and has a knack for being in the right place at the right time for club and country.

‌



‌



Despite that, he has started just once in the Premier League this season. Merino has averaged 49.9 minutes per appearance over the past 18 months, with his limited involvement fuelling speculation over his future at the Emirates.

‌



Spanish outlet La Razon (via Sport Witness) claims Atletico Madrid are interested in signing him on loan with an option to buy. The 30-year-old's contract runs until the summer of 2028, meaning Arsenal would enter the final year of his deal next summer.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

His father, Angel Miguel, recently discussed the prospect of a return to Spain. He said: "If he comes to La Liga, well, I suppose he’ll want to continue in that rhythm of competing in the Champions League and keeping that motivation, but obviously he’s in a comfortable situation there at Arsenal, isn’t he? Because he’s experiencing exactly what he wanted when he left Real Sociedad.”

‌



Merino is keen to represent Spain at Euro 2028, but regular club football could be crucial to retaining his place in Luis de la Fuente’s squad - increasing the prospetcs of a transfer. Despite his limited game time, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta remains a firm admirer of the midfielder.

"He’s unbelievable," the Arsenal boss said. "First of all, he’s one of the most intelligent players that I’ve seen and I’ve worked with.

‌



"Then the personality is just full of… I don’t know, he just wants to give for everybody. He thinks about everything, he thinks about everybody."

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has a decision to make regarding Mikel Merino

‌



He added: "He has qualities that are unique in football and in our team, his capacity to arrive in the box, he’s capable of occupying different places, to play in different positions, to link play with people.

"And as a midfielder, the ability that he has to score goals like tonight is a different one that we’ve seen lately, but another incredible one."

‌



Merino, signed by Arsenal from Real Sociedad in 2024 in a deal worth just under £32million, has 16 goals and eight assists under Arteta.

He often scores important goals, too, and his versatility proved invaluable in the 2024/25 season when a striker injury crisis meant the Spaniard was deployed as an emergency No.9.
