World.title: Ex-Air Force spokesperson identifies ‘flaw’ affecting Nigeria’s multi-trillion naira defence budget
World.content:
A former Nigerian Air Force spokesperson, Sadeeq Shehu, has faulted Nigeria’s defence budget structure, stating that poor planning and governance, rather than inadequate funding, are weakening the country’s security operations.

Mr Shehu, a retired group captain, made the assessment during an interview on ARISE News, monitored by PREMIUM TIMES, on Thursday, while examining the federal government’s special security interventions and defence allocations between 2023 and 2026.

He said that increasing military expenditure would not necessarily improve Nigeria’s security situation unless the government addressed how available resources were planned, allocated and utilised.

The retired officer said Nigeria was spending a reasonable proportion of its resources on defence but was failing to translate the expenditure into commensurate operational capacity.

“If you ask me, proportionate to what Nigeria is earning from its foreign trade and everything from petrol, I think we are spending right as far as amount is concerned. The problem is the plan and where do we put the money. The problem is also a governance issue,” he said.

His assessment comes on the heels of sustained security challenges across the country, including insurgency, banditry and other forms of violent crime, despite substantial government allocations to the defence and security sectors.

Mr Shehu identified the composition of the 2026 defence budget as evidence of the problem, saying an overwhelming proportion of the allocation was committed to personnel expenses at the expense of critical military requirements.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, the N3.154 trillion defence allocation provides N2.4 trillion, representing 75.9 per cent, for personnel costs, while overhead expenditure accounts for 9.4 per cent, or about N297 billion.

He questioned how the military could adequately provide equipment, maintain existing platforms, train personnel and modernise its operations when such a substantial proportion of its budget was absorbed by personnel costs.

“This is where the major problem is. And I do not see either the executive branch or even the legislature attacking this,” he said.

The former air force spokesperson argued that Nigeria’s defence budget needed a more detailed classification to reveal how much was being committed to specific military requirements.

He said the existing practice of grouping expenditure under personnel, overhead and capital costs obscured the actual funding available for equipment procurement, maintenance, training, military infrastructure and research.

He maintained that more detailed defence budgeting systems provide clearer expenditure categories, enabling governments to identify operational gaps and direct resources towards priority requirements.

“What global best practice has shown us is that the only thing that comes out from this budget is personnel cost. You will wonder, where is equipment? Where is maintenance? Where is training? A paltry less than 25 per cent is allocated to the two of them. This is not good enough,” he said.

Mr Shehu warned that without proper planning, Nigeria could continue spending substantial amounts on defence without adequately addressing the military’s most pressing operational needs.

He said a poorly structured budget could leave essential requirements unfunded while directing scarce resources towards less critical areas.

“If you don’t plan your defence budget properly, you are likely to leave things that are essential and put money where they are not essential. That is the point I want to make,” he said.

He also questioned the capacity of the presidency and the National Assembly to effectively scrutinise defence expenditure, arguing that the existing budget structure did not provide sufficient details for informed oversight.

According to him, lawmakers and government officials need a clearer understanding of the military’s operational requirements to ensure that budget allocations reflect actual security priorities.

“If you just leave it into these three, you know, three subheads, personnel, capital and overhead, you will never get the proper picture. And I can assure you from my research, the National Assembly and even the presidency, they do not have really a clear picture of what the defence budget is all about,” he said.

Mr Shehu’s position suggests that Nigeria’s challenge may be beyond how much it spends on defence, but whether the expenditure is structured to deliver the equipment, training, maintenance and operational capacity required to confront the country’s security threats.

He maintained that improving defence planning and governance, rather than merely increasing military allocations, should be central to efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s security operations.

World.title: Six journalists begin six-month fellowship to scrutinise development efforts in Niger Delta
World.content:
Six journalists from media organisations across Nigeria have begun a six-month fellowship to investigate development interventions, economic opportunities and efforts to address longstanding challenges in the Niger Delta.

The programme, launched on 2 November by the Foundation for Partnership Initiatives in the Niger Delta (PIND) and the School of Media and Communication (SMC), Pan-Atlantic University, is designed to strengthen development journalism and encourage more evidence-based reporting on the oil-rich region.

The initiative comes as development organisations, governments and private-sector actors continue to implement interventions in the Niger Delta, where continuous unemployment, insecurity, environmental degradation and limited economic opportunities have shaped public discourse about the region.

However, PIND said media coverage has often given limited attention to solutions, innovations and measurable development outcomes emerging from communities across the region.

The fellowship, known as the PIND Media Fellows Programme for Narrative Change in the Niger Delta, will combine specialised training, field immersion, access to development evidence and editorial mentorship.

It is expected to equip participating journalists to independently examine interventions in areas including peacebuilding, agriculture, youth employment, renewable energy and economic inclusion.

The programme opened with a five-day residential Impact Journalism Academy at SMC in Lagos, running from 2 to 6 November. The training covers development reporting, solutions journalism, impact storytelling, ethical interviewing, multimedia production and evidence-based reporting.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

PIND Executive Director, Sam Daibo, said the initiative was conceived to address the limited attention given to development solutions and progress in the region.

“The Niger Delta’s challenges must be reported honestly, but they should not be its only story. Across the region, communities, businesses and development partners are advancing solutions in peacebuilding, agriculture, youth employment, renewable energy and economic inclusion. This fellowship will help journalists examine those efforts critically, independently and with the depth they deserve,” Mr Daibo said.

He stressed that the programme was not intended to influence editorial decisions or encourage favourable coverage of PIND’s activities.

“Our role is to give journalists greater access to evidence, communities and development practice while respecting their editorial independence. Credible development reporting must remain rigorous, balanced and accountable to the public,” he added.

Ikechukwu Obiaya, dean of SMC, said the partnership would help journalists move beyond reporting activities to examining whether development interventions were delivering tangible results.

“Development journalism requires more than reporting activities. Journalists must be able to interrogate evidence, understand systems, centre community voices and determine whether interventions are producing meaningful change,” he said.

He said the training would combine development journalism skills with practical reporting tools that participants could apply in their newsrooms and field assignments.

PIND’s development interventions

The fellowship draws on PIND’s longstanding development interventions across the Niger Delta, particularly its economic development and peacebuilding programmes.

Established in 2010, the organisation works across the region’s nine states through partnerships with governments, businesses, civil society organisations and communities.

Under its economic development programme, PIND supports agricultural value chains, youth employment, access to finance and renewable energy.

The organisation says its interventions have reached more than 598,000 farmers and microenterprises with improved agricultural practices and market linkages, trained more than 11,000 young people in vocational skills and facilitated access to clean energy for more than 14,000 households and businesses.

Its peacebuilding programme also supports grassroots conflict prevention, community peace structures and initiatives aimed at strengthening collaboration among stakeholders.

An impact evaluation of PIND’s interventions conducted by international consulting firm Dalberg in 2023 found that the organisation’s economic development and peacebuilding activities had facilitated 86,713 jobs and helped mitigate 1,469 conflicts in the Niger Delta. The evaluation examined interventions implemented since 2016.

Some of its recent interventions include partnerships to expand solar mini-grids in underserved communities, support climate-smart agriculture, improve youth employability and strengthen agricultural markets.

In August 2026, PIND, Okomu Oil and ETIN Power commissioned a solar mini-grid in Gbelebu community, while the organisation has also supported solar-powered cold storage facilities to reduce post-harvest losses among farmers in Bayelsa State.

READ ALSO: Group calls for withdrawal of charges against Kaduna journalist

The fellowship will give journalists opportunities to examine such interventions, interact with programme beneficiaries and technical experts, and independently assess their outcomes.

Following the academy, the fellows will undertake field immersion, develop reporting pitches and receive editorial mentorship during the production of their stories.

The six journalists selected for the inaugural cohort are Ekemini Simon of PREMIUM TIMES, Ann Godwin of The Guardian, Isaac Eranga of The Nigerian Observers, Joseph Kunde of TVC News, Kpono-Abasi Jackson of Akwa Ibom Broadcasting Corporation and Jennifer Orugbo of Delta Broadcasting Service.

Beyond the initial six-month programme, PIND and SMC said they intend to establish successive cohorts and build a network of journalists committed to rigorous, balanced and evidence-driven reporting on the Niger Delta.

The initiative marks an attempt to move beyond occasional media engagements towards sustained investment in journalists’ capacity to interrogate development interventions and communicate their actual impact.

World.title: Peter Obi blames APC for court judgement sacking Atiku, David Mark
World.content:
The 2027 presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has faulted the court judgement that sacked the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and nullified the candidacy of all its aspirants for the 2027 elections. Mr Obi also accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of being responsible for the court ruling.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday declared as illegal, the David Mark-led Caretaker Committee, which conducted the ADC’s presidential primary that produced ex-Vice President Atiku Abubakar as its flag bearer.

The court also sacked the entire national officers of the party, including National Secretary Rauf Aregbesola, alongside all the candidates the party presented to the Independent National Electoral Commission for the 2027 elections.

‘Surprising and unsettling’

Reacting in an X post on Thursday evening, Mr Obi said he received the report of the court judgement with “shock.”

“This is unsettling and surprising,” he said of the judgement.

The NDC candidate said that while he did not dispute the court’s ruling, he was concerned that the development had occurred just months before the 2027 general elections.

“The court of law is constituted to determine disputes according to the law. My concern is that three months before a general election, it is in the public interest to have certainty.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“It is not good to have too many uncertainties about candidates and parties a few weeks before a presidential election,” he said.

The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for 16 January 2027, while governorship elections and state assembly polls are billed to be held on 6 February the same year.

‘APC engineered it’

Mr Obi accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of “engineering” the court ruling and leadership dispute in the ADC.

“This instability is obviously engineered by the ruling party, just as they have done against me in the Labour Party and continue to do so to close down civic space for a robust campaign.

“It is also from the same rulebook that manufactures violence against us in our campaigns,” he claimed without evidence.

Mr Obi was the presidential candidate of the Labour Party in 2023.

PREMIUM TIMES recalls that the Labour Party had suffered an intense leadership crisis shortly after the 2023 election, which many believe resulted in Mr Obi’s defection to the ADC in December 2025.

‘Don’t undermine democracy’

In the post on X, Mr Obi suggested that the ruling party was clamping down on opposition parties and called for the protection of democratic principles, warning against any attempt to undermine voters’ freedom to freely and fairly choose their preferred candidates.

“One mark of democracy is that at all times, it is voters and not courts that choose leaders.

“The sustenance of democracy in Nigeria, in the midst of encroaching military rule in West Africa, should strengthen our resolve to protect opposition politics and not stamp out opposition parties,” he said.

The NDC candidate stressed that it was because of the importance of opposition to democracy that he promised to ensure that opposition parties and their candidates were not persecuted out of electoral contests.

“This is a time to strengthen our democracy by allowing the opposition to thrive,” he said.

APC reacts

When contacted by PREMIUM TIMES on Thursday night, the spokesperson of the APC, Felix Morka, rejected Mr Obi’s claim that the ruling party engineered the court ruling and the crisis in the ADC.

“How come every time that a court gives a decision that’s unfavourable to them, they blame APC, but when it’s in their favour they hail the rule of law and extol the judiciary,” Mr Morka said.

The APC spokesperson stressed that if the judgement was in favour of the ADC, opposition politicians would not have been blaming the ruling party for the court’s decision.

“Tomorrow, I’ll issue a statement on this (allegation),” he added.

World.title: EFCC investigates ex-banker over alleged N515 million diversion
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) is investigating a former bank operations manager, Obinna Nwaobi, over the alleged diversion of N515 million from an account belonging to a customer, DAHUA Paper Company.

According to a statement from EFCC spokesperson Dele Oyewale on Thursday, the commission received a petition at its Enugu zonal from the bank on 22 June, alleging that the money was withdrawn from the company’s Debt Service Reserve Account (DSRA) without authorisation.

The withdrawals, according to the petition, were made in three transactions of N200 million, N150 million and N165 million on 17 July 2024.

The bank alleged that the transactions were processed at its Okpara Avenue branch in Enugu using forged documents and authorised by Mr Nwaobi, who was then its head of operations.

It said the account had been reactivated in June 2024 but was not placed on a Post No Debit (PND) restriction, which should have prevented withdrawals.

The EFCC stated that preliminary investigations showed that the account was opened for the repayment of a Bank of Industry loan and was not meant for ordinary transactions.

It said withdrawals or transfers to third parties from such accounts require approval from the account officer, regional manager and credit monitoring team. The commission alleged that the N515 million transactions were carried out without the required approvals.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The investigation comes as Mr Nwaobi is also facing trial on charges of diverting $510,000 belonging to another customer of Access Bank, Lantern Gate Nigeria Limited.

He was arraigned before the Federal High Court in Enugu in November 2025 on nine charges of forgery and criminal diversion.

The EFCC alleged that the money was transferred to six different accounts without the customer’s approval. One of the charges accused Mr Nwaobi of inducing the bank to transfer the funds on the false pretence that Lantern Gate had authorised the transactions.

He pleaded not guilty to the charges. The court granted him bail in the sum of N250 million, with three sureties in like sum, and adjourned the case to 10, 11 and 12 March 2026 for trial.

The EFCC did not name the bank involved in the latest N515 million allegation, although it said the transactions were processed through its Okpara Avenue branch in Enugu.

The commission said Mr Nwaobi would be charged in connection with the latest allegation after investigations are concluded.

World.title: Why I separated from my wife – Actor Kunle Afod
World.content:
Nollywood actor Kunle Afod has spoken about the circumstances leading to the breakdown of his marriage to Desola, whom he married in 2005.

Reports about the couple’s separation emerged in February after claims surfaced that Desola moved her belongings out of their matrimonial home.

However, neither Afod nor Desola addressed the reports publicly or confirmed the separation until the actor spoke about it during an interview on Kasnasty Sugar, posted on YouTube on Thursday.

Although Afod did not offer a detailed account of what transpired between them, he identified jealousy, infidelity and trust issues as some of the problems that affected their marriage.

Responding to questions about the separation, the actor spoke in parables but suggested that both partners had cheated during the marriage.

He said: “Regarding the separation between my wife and me, my profession is so demanding that we hardly have time for our family. Do you want to hear the truth? I apologise to all the women here. People often accept that men cheat. However, no man cheats with a tree; he cheats with a woman.

“It is easier for a woman to be a lesbian than for a man to be gay. If you have a wife who is very close to her female friends, be careful because you could be in danger. Women cheat with other women more than they sleep with men who are not their husbands.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Sex toy

The actor further highlighted what he perceived as unequal expectations between partners over the use of bedroom toys.

He wondered why a woman would have no reservations about asking her husband to buy them for her but would object to finding out that he also uses them.

“It is easy for a woman to persuade her husband to buy her a dildo because she claims she does not want to cheat. She will buy the first, second and even third dildo, but what she is doing amounts to cheating with a sex toy.

“Why is she not satisfied with just one dildo? That, too, can be regarded as adultery. The same woman who confidently uses a dildo may not take it lightly if she catches her husband using sex toys, he added.

The estranged couple started their relationship in 2002 and exchanged marital vows in 2005. The marriage produced children.

World.title: Poor financial records, cash flow woes crippling Nigerian businesses — SWAN
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

LAGOS — The Society of Women Accountants of Nigeria (SWAN) has identified poor financial record-keeping, inadequate cash flow management, ineffective pricing and limited understanding of profitability as some of the factors undermining the survival and growth of businesses in Nigeria.

The association said many promising businesses struggle not necessarily because of a lack of opportunities or customers, but because their owners lack the financial knowledge required to manage resources and make informed decisions.

SWAN stated this at its 2026 Accounting for Non-Accountants Workshop, held on Thursday at the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN) Annex, Ebute-Metta, Lagos.

The workshop, organised as part of the association’s Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives, had the theme, “Business Made Easy: Practical Financial Skills.”

Speaking at the event, Chairperson of the Planning Committee, Mrs Ruth Jawo, said financial literacy had become essential for entrepreneurs, traders, professionals, employees and business managers, particularly amid the country’s challenging economic conditions.

According to her, financial knowledge would enable business owners to make informed decisions, manage resources effectively, avoid penalties and achieve sustainable growth.

“The theme reflects SWAN’s commitment to simplifying financial concepts and equipping participants with practical knowledge,” she said.

Jawo explained that the workshop was designed to bridge existing financial knowledge gaps and empower participants to manage their finances more confidently.

She expressed the expectation that participants would apply the knowledge acquired to improve their businesses, workplaces and households.

“Our expectation is that every participant leaves with valuable knowledge, practical tools and a renewed determination to develop better financial habits.

“The true success of this workshop will be measured not merely by attendance, but by the positive changes it inspires in businesses, workplaces and households,” she said.

Jawo urged participants to put the lessons into practice, describing the workshop as an opportunity to promote financial empowerment and sustainable growth.

She also commended SWAN’s leadership, facilitators, sponsors, partners, planning committee members and volunteers for their contributions to the programme.

Earlier, the National Chairperson of SWAN, Mrs Blessing Osakwe-Ogo, challenged participants to consider why businesses that record daily sales could still struggle to meet their financial obligations.

She said the problem was often not a shortage of customers, but inadequate financial records and the inability of business owners to interpret them.

“You cannot successfully grow what you do not properly measure, and you cannot protect a business whose financial position you do not understand,” she said.

Osakwe-Ogo explained that the programme was designed to equip entrepreneurs and business owners with practical knowledge of basic bookkeeping and accounting records.

She said the skills would help them track income and expenditure, monitor profitability, control costs and make informed business decisions.

The SWAN chairperson added that the association had expanded the programme to include discussions on emerging financial and tax laws, particularly Nigeria’s recent tax reforms and their implications for small businesses, entrepreneurs and business owners.

The workshop featured presentations by various facilitators on practical financial management skills.

World.title: $2bn Afreximbank fund targets Africa’s creative economy as CANEX opens in Lagos
World.content:
By Elizabeth Onyogha

Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) WKND 2026 opened in Lagos yesterday, bringing together leading creatives, investors, policymakers, business leaders and cultural figures from across Africa and the diaspora to explore investment, financing and commercial opportunities in the continent’s creative economy.



Hosted by the Federal Government of Nigeria and organised by the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) through its Creative Africa Nexus programme, the four-day event runs from November 5 to 8 under the theme, “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World.”

The programme covers film and television, music, fashion, sport, literature and publishing, gastronomy and visual arts, with emphasis on financing, intellectual property, technology, skills development, investment and market access.

Through platforms such as the CANEX Deal Room and Creative Pitch Sessions, the event seeks to connect entrepreneurs with financiers and investors, turning creative ideas and talent into viable businesses, partnerships and commercial opportunities.

The initiative builds on Afreximbank’s commitment to Africa’s creative and cultural industries, which began in 2020 and has since expanded to $2 billion in available financing.

The funding is designed to help African creators and businesses develop scalable enterprises, strengthen ownership of intellectual property and retain more of the economic value generated by the continent’s cultural and creative industries.

The opening ceremony is expected to feature addresses by ministers responsible for culture and creative industries from 11 African countries; Dr. George Elombi, President and Chairman of the Board of Directors of Afreximbank; Dr. Olajumoke Omoniyi Oduwole, Nigeria’s Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment; Wamkele Mene, Secretary-General of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat; and Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Governor of Lagos State, among other dignitaries.

Participants include Nobel Laureate, writer and playwright, Professor Wole Soyinka; Emmy Award-winning actor Uzo Aduba; filmmaker and actor Funke Akindele; actors Richard Mofe-Damijo and Thuso Mbedu; and former professional footballers Didier Drogba and Jay-Jay Okocha.

Musicians and entertainers, including Davido, Fally Ipupa, Flavour, Libianca and Charlotte Dipanda, are also scheduled to perform.

On November 6, a high-level conversation titled “One Market, One Culture: Building the Creative Economy of Global Africa” will examine how to translate the growing global influence of African culture into stronger creative businesses, exports and investment.

Speakers will include Soyinka; ministers responsible for culture and the arts from Côte d’Ivoire, South Africa and Rwanda; representatives of the International Finance Corporation; and Afreximbank officials.

Financing will also take centre stage at the Creative Economy Finance Summit, organised by Afreximbank in partnership with the Creative Economy Practice at Co-Creation Hub.

The summit will bring financial institutions and investors together to examine how creative-economy transactions can be structured, financed and de-risked.

CANEX Creations Inc. will lead discussions on unlocking investment in African intellectual property, while technology-focused sessions will examine artificial intelligence, authorship, intellectual property and the use of digital tools to develop globally competitive creative products.

The CANEX CreaThon, organised in partnership with pan-African technology company Gebeya, will bring creators, developers and innovators together to develop projects in music, video and gaming. Participants will have access to digital tools, mentorship and computing resources, alongside a $50,000 prize pool.

Film and television sessions will explore storytelling and the commercial infrastructure required to distribute African content internationally. These include “Stories Without Borders: Africa, Hollywood & the Global Diaspora,” featuring former Afreximbank President, Professor Benedict Oramah, and “Made in Africa, watched in Africa,” which will examine research on film distribution, audiences and financing across Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal and South Africa.

Sport will feature prominently, with discussions on athlete development, management and commercialisation. Drogba and Okocha are scheduled to participate in “When Giants Speak: The Business of the Game,” while a Legends Football Match will hold at Onikan Stadium on November 8.

Fashion activities will include masterclasses on building profitable African brands, strengthening textile value chains, expanding market access and protecting intellectual property, alongside the CANEX Fashion Show and Awards Night.

In gastronomy, the CANEX Junior Chefs Competition, Africa Jollof Wars Competition and live demonstrations will explore opportunities to commercialise African food, ingredients and culinary traditions in domestic and international markets.

Publishing and literature activities will feature the CANEX Book Factory, Book Fair, writers’ workshops, manuscript pitching sessions and the CANEX Prize for Publishing.

Visual arts programming will include exhibitions, collector engagement and practical sessions for artists.

On November 7, the event will host a major concert featuring performers from across Africa and the diaspora.

The final day, November 8, will feature cultural excursions, gastronomy activities, the CANEX Music Factory Songwriting Camp and the Legends Football Match.

World.title: REA flags off 18.8MW mini-grid projects to connect 125,106 Zamfara households
World.content:
By Udeme Akpan

The Rural Electrification Agency (REA) has flagged off the development of 37 mini-grid projects with a combined solar generation capacity of approximately 18.8 megawatts-peak (MWp) in Zamfara State.



The projects, comprising two interconnected and 35 isolated mini-grids, are expected to connect 125,106 households across Gummi, Gusau, Kaura Namoda, Maradun, Shinkafi, Tsafe and Zurmi Local Government Areas.



The groundbreaking ceremony on Wednesday also featured the unveiling of the Zamfara State Electricity Policy and the signing of a collaboration agreement between REA and the state government for the solarisation of public institutions.



Speaking at the event, Governor Dauda Lawal described the initiatives as important steps towards building an investment-friendly electricity market and accelerating economic development.



“Today, we are taking deliberate steps to redefine Zamfara’s electricity future. The unveiling of our State Electricity Policy is a statement of our intention to build a structured, investment-friendly and sustainable electricity market,” he said.



Lawal said reliable electricity was essential for agricultural transformation, industrial development, healthcare delivery, education and job creation.



Also speaking, the Minister of Power, Chief Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe, said the projects demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to expanding electricity access through decentralised infrastructure, state-level market development and private-sector investment.



“Electricity must do more than illuminate homes. It must power hospitals, strengthen educational institutions, support agricultural productivity, enable businesses and improve the quality of public services,” Tegbe said.



He pledged continued Federal Government support for states taking practical steps to develop their electricity markets.

In his remarks, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of REA, Dr. Abba Aliyu, said the intervention marked a shift from isolated infrastructure projects to an integrated electricity development model.



“Through the REA, we are advancing 37 mini-grid projects comprising two interconnected and 35 isolated systems, with approximately 18.8MWp of solar generation capacity and 125,106 planned electricity connections across seven Local Government Areas,” he said.



Aliyu estimated that the connections could potentially reach more than 625,000 people, based on an illustrative average of five persons per household-equivalent connection.



He said the initiative would support businesses, strengthen agricultural value chains, create jobs and attract private investment.

“Infrastructure without an enabling market framework risk becoming a collection of disconnected assets. When electricity infrastructure is supported by clear policies, effective institutions and predictable investment conditions, it becomes the foundation of a sustainable electricity economy,” he added.



Aliyu said the projects aligned with the $750 million World Bank-supported Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-up (DARES) programme, which targets electricity access for approximately 17.5 million Nigerians through about 1,350 mini-grids and other distributed renewable energy solutions.



Meanwhile, Tegbe commissioned two solar mini-grid projects developed by the Zamfara State Government: a 1MW facility at Yariman Bakura Specialist Hospital and a 1.2MW installation at the Zamfara State Government House. Together, they have 2.2MW generation capacity and more than 3MW of battery storage.



The event also featured the unveiling of 100 electric vehicles under the ZamTaxi initiative, 10 electric tricycles for maternal healthcare transportation and two compressed natural gas buses donated by the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas.

World.title: Malaria, TB Diagnosis: Global Fund Trains 464 Lab personnel in 9 States
World.content:
… Experts say poor tests fuel malaria misdiagnosis

By Chioma Obinna

Poor laboratory testing, inaccurate malaria diagnosis and unnecessary prescription of antimalarial drugs remain major challenges undermining Nigeria’s fight against malaria, health experts have warned.



The experts spoke as the Global Fund supported the training of 464 laboratory personnel across nine states to strengthen malaria and tuberculosis (TB) diagnosis, improve disease surveillance and ensure reliable laboratory results.



The integrated capacity-building programme, implemented through the National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP) and the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, was inaugurated at Mokland Hotel, Ibara, GRA, Abeokuta, Ogun State.



Speaking at the event, Consultant Medical Parasitologist, College of Medicine, University of Lagos, Professor Wellington Oyibo, said accurate diagnosis was critical to effective treatment, warning that laboratory personnel must be equipped to identify different malaria parasite species and distinguish infections from other illnesses.



He said microscopy remained essential despite the availability of rapid diagnostic tests and molecular technologies, stressing the need for quality assurance, proper documentation and timely reporting.



Oyibo said participants would be trained in slide preparation, microscopy, parasite identification, quality management and diagnostic best practices, including standards under ISO 15189.



He said the programme was designed to produce a critical mass of competent laboratory professionals who would also mentor colleagues in their respective facilities.



In a troubling revelation, Ogun State Malaria Elimination Programme Manager, Mrs Olamide Adeyinka, said patients’ insistence on having malaria despite negative test results was contributing to inappropriate treatment and unreliable malaria statistics.

She explained that some patients pressured health workers into prescribing antimalarial drugs even when laboratory investigations showed otherwise.

She said, “We have always recorded a high malaria test positivity rate, but many of these cases are linked to the failure to conduct proper tests or patients refusing to accept test results.”

Adeyinka disclosed that participants were drawn from all 20 local government areas of Ogun State, covering primary, secondary and tertiary health facilities, as well as private and faith-based institutions.

Also, Assistant Director, Medical Laboratory Services, Ogun State, Dr Simon Ijiezie, warned that inaccurate diagnosis was exposing people without malaria to unnecessary medication and financial losses.

He appealed to the state government to provide quality laboratory equipment, particularly microscopes, to ensure that the training translates into improved services.

“Without a good microscope, accurate diagnosis becomes difficult,” he said.

The Assistant Director, Medical Laboratory Services, Ogun State Primary Health Care Board, Mr Atinsola Ayodeji Olalekan, said strengthening primary healthcare laboratories would reduce pressure on secondary and tertiary hospitals.

“We believe that when primary healthcare facilities get things right, there will be less pressure on higher levels of healthcare institutions,” he said.

On tuberculosis diagnosis, the State TB Quality Assurance Officer, Mr Ogundimu Olusola, representing the state TB Programme Manager, Dr Jimoh Babatunde, warned that the growing use of molecular diagnostic technologies had reduced interest in microscopy among some laboratory workers.

“With the introduction of molecular diagnostic methods, some people have gradually lost interest in microscopy,” he said.

He expressed confidence that the training would produce 44 re-energised and better-equipped personnel in Ogun State.

Meanwhile, Assistant Director, Medical Laboratory Services, Hospital Management Board, Ogun State, Mrs Adebola Oke, urged participants to transfer their knowledge to colleagues after the programme.

“When you light a candle, you do not put it under a basket. You place it where it can illuminate the entire room,” she said.

The training, which also features intensive practical sessions, has already improved participants’ confidence in identifying malaria parasites, including Plasmodium malariae.

World.title: Don’t allow yourself be used to stifle democracy, NDC to Judiciary
World.content:
By Henry Umoru

The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC has urged the judiciary not to allow itself to be used to stifle the nation’s democracy.

The party has cautioned the judiciary to guard its independence, impartiality, and integrity at all times.

The NDC said while it respects the judiciary as the last hope of the common man, it is concerned as a party that judgments of this nature, if not carefully handled, would at the end of the day risk creating the impression that the courts are being used to scuttle democracy and weaken opposition.

In a statement signed late Thursday night by the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, he said the way and manner some of these judgements are being churned out, especially from the High Courts suggests a deliberate effort to shut out the ADC from the forthcoming general elections by other means.

According to Director, if not checked, this would amount to further shrinking the chances of multi-party democracy which is already under a big threat under the APC-led government of President Bola Tinubu.

Recall that the Federal High Court in Abuja had sacked the Senator David Mark-led executives of the African Democratic

Congress (ADC) and invalidated all actions they took on behalf of the party.

The actions included the nomination of a former vice president, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections.Track Exec Orders.

Atiku, whose name was earlier published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as a candidate for the presidential poll, has since chosen a former governor of Rivers State, Rotimi Amaechi, as his running mate.Track Exec Orders

In the judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu, the court declared illegal the Senator Mark-led Caretaker Committee of the ADC, which organised the primary election that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential flag bearer.

While reacting to the judgement of the court against the David Mark led leadership of the ADC, the NDC National Publicity Secretary said, “We have noted the Federal High Court judgment derecognizing the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

“While we respect the judiciary as the last hope of the common man, we are concerned that judgments of this nature, if not carefully handled, risk creating the impression that the courts are being used to scuttle democracy and weaken opposition.

“The way some of these judgements are being churned out, especially from the High Courts suggests a deliberate effort to shut out the ADC from the forthcoming general elections by other means. This would amount to further shrinking the chances of multi-party democracy which is already under a big threat under the APC-led government of President Bola Ahmed

Tinubu.

“We therefore caution the judiciary to guard its independence, impartiality, and integrity at all times.

“We urge the ADC to appeal the judgment without delay and call on the appellate court to grant an accelerated hearing in view of the fast-approaching 2027 general elections, so that uncertainty does not undermine democratic participation. A New Nigeria is POssible!

World.title: 2027: Tinubu, T. Y. Danjuma, Northeast, North-Central leaders meet in Aso Villa
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

Ahead of January 16, 2027 presidential election, the former Minister of Defence, General Theophilus Danjuma (retd) and political leaders from the Northeast and North-Central geopolitical zones yesterday, met behind closed doors with President Bola Tinubu at the Aso Villa, Abuja.

The meeting it was gathered was part of have consultations aimed at mobilising support for the President.

The meeting focused on forging political cooperation, security and other issues affecting their communities, just as the visitors said there have been remarkable improvements in security and the administration’s contributions to the development of their communities.

The delegation was made up of the Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang; his Taraba State counterpart, Agbu Kefas; former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Yakubu Dogara; Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd); and National Chairman of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentanwe Yilwatda.

Speaking with journalists after the meeting, Dogara disclosed that the delegation visited the President to express solidarity with his administration and explore strategies for strengthening political support for him across their communities.

He said the consultations were particularly significant as political activities gathered momentum ahead of the next general elections.

According to him: “We’re all here to show solidarity to Mr. President and then, in the spirit of the season, which you know is all about politicking, to discuss matters that affect our community and how we can best help in mobilising support for the President, who has done so much for our community.

“That is basically the reason why we’re here.”

The former House of Representatives Speaker expressed satisfaction with what he described as remarkable improvements in the security situation across parts of the country previously affected by insurgency, banditry and other violent crimes.

He said, although isolated security challenges persist, sustained government interventions have considerably reduced the frequency and severity of attacks in several troubled areas.

He recalled the dangerous security situation along the Abuja-Kaduna corridor, where travellers previously faced frequent attacks and kidnappings, noting that the situation had substantially improved.

“The issues relating to insecurity that accentuated over time, we have noticed that there is remarkable decline in these issues.

“Of course, there are pockets of crisis in some places, short of declaring victory, but there has been remarkable improvement.

“To travel from here to Kaduna, everybody knows what it was. At a point, they even brought down a moving train, but right now, some of those crises are not there”, he said.

Dogara attributed some of the improvements to the contributions of capable individuals appointed into strategic positions in the administration, particularly those familiar with the security challenges confronting affected communities.

He expressed optimism that continued commitment to the current interventions would produce more sustainable peace and stability.

“We believe that through some strategic placement of our sons and daughters within the government, they have shown remarkable leadership in dealing with these challenges.

“We believe that if these efforts are sustained going forward, we will arrive at a place where most of us will be very, very comfortable”, Dogara added.

Also speaking, Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, said political and community leaders in his state were making significant progress in rebuilding trust and promoting reconciliation among communities previously divided by ethnic and religious tensions.

He explained that the renewed engagement among leaders was beginning to encourage similar cooperation at the grassroots, particularly among young people.

“We are making tremendous progress, trying to make sure that leaders come together at various levels to rebuild the broken walls of trust, to rebuild understanding.

“Once people begin to see that kind of cohesion among leaders, it inspires them. It cascades down, and so this is what we are doing at the moment”, the governor said.

Mutfwang noted that political leaders on the Plateau were deliberately demonstrating unity through regular engagement and consistent messages encouraging peaceful coexistence.

He said the approach was beginning to yield encouraging results, with youth leaders from different ethnic and religious backgrounds initiating dialogue independently of government intervention.

“I believe that for us on the Plateau, those of us who are in the front lines of leadership are trying to demonstrate that by being seen together, by saying the same things, urging people to unite, to come together.

“People are taking responsibility, even among the youths. We are seeing a new vista in that direction, where youth leaders across the divides of faith and ethnicity are beginning to have conversations without even government support”, he stated.

Describing the development as a significant breakthrough in the state’s peacebuilding efforts, Mutfwang expressed confidence that sustained dialogue, cooperation and responsible leadership would help overcome longstanding divisions.

“This is quite encouraging to me that there is light at the end of the tunnel, and by the grace of God, we will continue to sustain these initiatives.

“Hopefully, a lot of the things that have happened in the past will become stories of the past, and we will be able to build a better, stable and prosperous future”, the governor said.

World.title: Bournemouth stay perfect in Europa League as Milan lose again
World.content:
Sparta Praha’s Norwegian midfielder #20 Sivert Mannsverk (C-R) and Bournemouth’s Moroccan forward #21 Amine Adli (C-L) vie for the ball during the UEFA Europa League football match between AC Sparta Praha and AFC Bournemouth in Prague on November 5, 2026. (Photo by Michal Cizek / AFP)

Bournemouth extended their perfect Europa League record on Thursday as they came from behind to win 3-1 at 10-man Sparta Prague, while Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan suffered a third defeat in four matches.

Gambian Ebrima Singhateh ran from his own half to score a fine individual goal as Sparta took the lead in the Czech Republic after Bournemouth midfielder Lewis Cook hit the post with a first-half penalty.

Sparta had Tobias Guddal sent off before half-time and Bournemouth equalised through Tyler Adams on 57 minutes.

Evanilson steered the Cherries ahead nine minutes from time and Rayan bagged a late third as Bournemouth’s substitutes sent the European newcomers top of the table with a fourth successive victory.

Marco Rose’s side have won each of their past seven matches in all competitions ahead of a Premier League trip to Ipswich this weekend.

“It’s a big achievement and we have to continue, we need to stay alert, sharp,” Rose told TNT Sports.

“It’s up to us to use this momentum. Everyone tries to beat us, if we get in a comfort zone just a little bit we get in trouble.”

Milan lost 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros as the Hungarians kept pace with Bournemouth, maintaining their 100 percent record in Europe.

Haiti international Lenny Joseph struck twice in the second half at San Siro to earn Ferencvaros a deserved win over the seven-time European champions despite having Bamidele Yusuf sent off.

“We gifted opportunities, made stupid errors. We were not prepared to play football tonight,” Amorim told Sky Sport.

“I don’t want to lie to my players. We cannot play like this in front of our own fans. It was a very poor performance.”

Milan are languishing outside the top 24 with just three points at the halfway stage of the league phase.

“I won’t give up on this competition. As long as we’re not mathematically out of it, we’ll keep fighting,” Amorim added.

Crystal Palace snatched a 1-1 draw at home to Hoffenheim as Japanese midfielder Daichi Kamada levelled in stoppage time.

Alexander Prass gave Hoffenheim an early lead at Selhurst Park and Palace lost Adam Wharton to a second yellow card before Kamada rescued a point for Pierre Sage’s struggling side.

Palace, last season’s UEFA Conference League winners, have five points from four outings in the Europa League but sit in the Premier League’s relegation zone, just behind Manchester United on goal difference.

World.title: Ebola patient flown to UK from DR Congo
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

A UK medic who tested positive for Ebola while working on the outbreak of the disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been flown to London for treatment, the government said Thursday.

The unnamed British citizen “has returned to the UK for specialist treatment after testing positive for the disease”, the government said in a statement.

Africa’s latest Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to the continent’s top health agency.

The British government said that the UK medic is now being treated at the Royal Free Hospital in London.

This hospital has a high-level isolation unit “specifically designed for this purpose” and strict protocols to prevent contact with the general public, it said.

Renu Bindra, deputy director of the all hazards public health response team at the UK health security agency (UKHSA) said “the risk to the wider public remains low”.

Last month, Nigeria reported an Ebola case involving a 42-year-old Swiss woman whose husband works at the country’s embassy. She was flown for treatment in Geneva.

World.title: Kwara Rebuilders Accuses PDP Guber Candidate, Kawu, of Plot to Restore Saraki Dynasty
World.content:
Sunday Ehigiator

A sociopolitical group, Kwara Rebuilders has accused the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Kwara State, Engr. Kale Kawu, of prioritising the restoration of the political dynasty of former Senate President, Bukola Saraki, over the interests of the people.

The group described Kawu’s alleged political commitment to Saraki as “ungodly and dead on arrival,” insisting that his ambition to govern the state was driven by a desire to revive the dynasty rather than serve the electorate.

In a statement issued yesterday by its Kwara Central Media Officer, AbdulQuadri AbdulKabeer, the group criticised Kawu and his media team for responding to earlier criticisms with grammatical explanations instead of addressing what it described as substantive questions about his political intentions and governance agenda.

Kwara Rebuilders said the response was an attempt to divert attention from concerns about Kawu’s alleged political loyalty to Saraki and accusations that he had copied and recycled previous manifestos.

“We consider the response of Kawu and his team as a mere academic exercise that does not treat the substantial issues,” the group said.

It maintained that Kawu had previously made his intentions clear in a video message, which it claimed showed that his governorship ambition was tied to restoring the Saraki political dynasty.

“His covenant is to Saraki, not the people of Kwara State. Kawu didn’t mince words in his earlier video message that his only motive for governorship is to restore and revive the Saraki dynasty, a dynasty where Kwara was ruled through proxy, with high-handedness and anyhowness being the order of the day,” the statement added.

The group also dismissed Kawu’s planned unveiling of a manifesto titled Covenant with Kwarans, describing it as an afterthought that would not convince voters.

It argued that the PDP candidate’s alleged commitment to Saraki contradicted the idea of a people-oriented political manifesto.

“The guber agenda is built on an undemocratic covenant with Saraki that he cannot deny,” it said.

Kwara Rebuilders further alleged that Kawu had pledged to restore the political dynasty and potentially use the state’s resources to advance Saraki’s reported 2031 presidential ambition.

It challenged the candidate to explain how such an alleged commitment could be reconciled with his proposed covenant with the people of Kwara.

“The point remains that Kawu’s narratives are inconsistent and conflicting. He has been caught on tape literally genuflecting while making good of his covenant to his leader, Senator Bukola Saraki, that his mission is to restore the dynasty and surrender the state’s purse to pursue his 2031 presidential ambition. Where on earth does covenant to a dynasty equal to covenant to Kwarans?” the group queried.

The organisation also drew parallels with previous political arrangements in the state, alleging that politicians who made similar commitments had eventually prioritised their political godfathers over the electorate.

It cited former Governor Abdulfatah Ahmed as an example, arguing that political promises and covenants had not always translated into accountability to the people.

The group urged voters to scrutinise Kawu’s political intentions, warning against entrusting the state’s leadership to a candidate it described as sycophantic.

It further claimed that Kwarans had rejected the Saraki political dynasty in two consecutive electoral cycles because of its alleged governance failures.

“Kwarans rejected the dynasty in two consecutive electoral cycles for its many failings and disasters. They are not ready to go back to their vomit, which is exactly what Kale Kawu is promising,” the statement said.

World.title: 2027: APP to Decide Between Tinubu, Atiku, Obi, Says Chairman
World.content:
National Chairman of the Action Peoples Party (APP), Barr. Uche Nnadi, has disclosed that the party is on the verge of announcing its preferred presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections.

Nnadi made this known following the party’s National Executive Council (NEC) meeting held in Abuja, where key issues concerning the party’s political direction and preparations for the 2027 polls were discussed.

According to the Chairman, the party is currently considering the major political contenders, including President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, and NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, as it moves towards taking a position on the forthcoming presidential election.

He further disclosed that a public announcement on the party’s preferred candidate is expected before the end of November, adding that the decision will be formally communicated at the party’s National Convention.

Nnadi also announced that the party’s National Convention and Campaign Rally, which will feature the formal presentation of its flag, will hold in Kaduna for the Northern region and Owerri for Southern Nigeria.

He explained that the planned events would provide the platform for the party to formally unveil its position and communicate its political direction ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The APP Chairman reiterated that the party’s leadership was committed to an inclusive decision-making process that would reflect the collective position of its stakeholders as it prepares for the next electoral cycle.

World.title: Peter Ikenga: Nigeria’s Power Sector Needs Self-sustaining Investment
World.content:
Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Transcorp Power Plc, Engr. Peter Ikenga, has said Nigeria’s power sector needs self-sustaining investment across its value chain to improve power supply, stating that the power generating company is committed to Nigeria’s power sector for the long term.

Ikenga spoke recently in Lagos as a panelist at the third edition of the Shell Power Conference, themed “Powering Nigeria’s Progress: Turning Ambition and Action into Sustainable Impact.”

He said Transcorp Power, one of the two power portfolio subsidiaries of Transcorp Group, will continue to sustain generation, invest in its plant and deliver value to shareholders despite a challenging operating environment.

“Transcorp Power is a long-term player, not a short-term player,” Ikenga said. “This year has been challenging, but what is important is getting power to schools, hospitals and businesses to power progress.”

According to him, the company’s focus on efficiency and investment underpins its contribution to the country’s power supply. “We run a highly efficient operation, and we have made significant investments to increase our available capacity, because we understand the value power has for development, progress and prosperity in Nigeria and West Africa.”

Ikenga noted that since acquiring the Ughelli Power Plant in Delta State in 2013, Transcorp Power has grown available capacity four folds.

Transcorp Power became the first privatised power generation company to receive a post-privatisation discharge certificate for fulfilling all its privatisation obligations. He said this discipline is reflected in the company’s unaudited results for the nine months ended 30 September 2026.

Transcorp Power recorded a profit before tax of ₦83.1 billion, while its profit-before-tax margin improved to 31.2% from 29.6% a year earlier. Total assets grew 11.7% to ₦629.5 billion, and shareholders’ funds rose 8.9% to ₦199.8 billion. Cash and cash equivalents increased to ₦10.3 billion, supported by improved collections. Speaking on the company’s role in grid stability, Transcorp Power MD/CEO said as a black-start provider, Transcorp Power can restart without external power from the grid. Following a disturbance, “this allows us to support restoration and help bring electricity back to homes, businesses and industries quickly.”

On the future of the sector, Ikenga noted that Nigeria has an installed generating capacity of about 13,000 megawatts and an estimated potential of 50 gigawatts, presenting significant room for growth.

He clarified that the potential requires every part of the value chain to work together. “Everything in the value chain has to work,” he said.

He called for sustained investment and collaboration among federal and state governments, the private sector and regulators, alongside increased private sector participation, to build a self-sustaining sector. He added that power generated at scale remains the most cost-effective route to industrialisation.

“Generating power at scale is beneficial because it is cheap. To industrialise, the grid is a proven system anywhere in the world,” he said.

He also urged stakeholders to join efforts to protect power infrastructure from vandalism. “We have to protect and secure what we have today in order to guaranty our future,” he said.

Expressing confidence in the sector’s prospects, Ikenga said: “The future is super great.”

He assured stakeholders that Transcorp Power will continue to invest in its operations, sustain generation and deliver superior value to its shareholders and to Nigeria.

World.title: PSC Approves Deployment of Four Police Commissioners to Plateau, Enugu, Nasarawa, Ondo
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the deployment of four Commissioners of Police (CPs) to various state commands following a series of interviews to assess their fitness and suitability for their new positions.

According to a statement by the Head of Protocol and Public Relations of the PSC, Torty Njoku Kalu, the postings are as follows: “CP Sunday J. A. Okoebor, formerly CP, Police Accounts and Budget, Force Headquarters, has been posted to Plateau State. CP Fidelis Ogarabe, formerly CP, INTERPOL Annex, Lagos, has been posted to Enugu State.

“CP Sheikh Mohammed Danko, formerly CP, Force Intelligence Annex, Lagos, has been posted to Nasarawa State, while CP Johnson Ayodeji Babalola, formerly CP, Special Inquiry, Force Headquarters, Abuja, has been posted to Ondo State as the Commissioner of Police.”

The Chairman of the commission, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd), while affirming the postings, noted that the redeployments were in line with the provisions of Section 215(1)(b) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, which empowers the commission to appoint Commissioners of Police for each state of the Federation and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The chairman, who was represented by a Board Member, Hon. Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (JSC rtd), said the interviews had established that the Commissioners of Police were worthy in learning and character.

He urged them to remain impartial and live up to the expectations of their new offices.

World.title: Tinubu Departs Abuja Friday For Two-state Visit To S’South
World.content:
.To attend APC campaign rallies In Akwa Ibom, Rivers

.Will also inaugurate some landmark projects of Gov Eno

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu will depart the nation’s capital, Abuja on Friday, November 6, for a two-state visit to Akwa Ibom and Rivers states.

The President, in a release issued on Thursday by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, will first visit Uyo, the Akwa Ibom State capital, to inaugurate landmark projects completed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration and attend a political rally.

Governor Eno, the host, has declared Friday a work-free day in the state to give the President a rousing reception.

Among the projects Tinubu is scheduled to inaugurate in Uyo are the new International Terminal Building, the International Airport Hospital, and the Ibom Aviation Village, all located at the Victor Attah International Airport.

The President will also inaugurate the Airport-Okopedi Road in Nsit Atai and Okobo Local Government Areas and Ring Road 3, linking Idoro Road to Ikot Ekpene Road through Uyo and Ibiono Ibom.

Other projects include the AKWA-GIS Office Complex, the Command and Control Centre and the ARISE Palm Resort.

On Saturday, Tinubu will leave for Port Harcourt, Rivers State, to take part in the All Progressives Congress rally.

The rally will be his third, since he flagged off the re-election campaign in Kaduna last month.

The visits will also give the President opportunities to engage with political stakeholders, party members, and supporters while emphasising unity, political stability, and a shared commitment to national progress.

World.title: Reps Subcommittee Dismisses Petition Seeking Cancellation Of NIPCO’s Gas Distribution Licences
World.content:
The House of Representatives Sub-Committee on the Petition concerning NIPCO Plc has dismissed a petition filed by the Nigerian Energy Security Watch Group (NESWG), which sought an investigation, suspension and cancellation of gas distribution licences issued to NIPCO Plc by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA).

The decision was reached on Thursday when the Sub-Committee, constituted in October 2026 to examine the petition, resolved not to proceed with the proposed investigation.

The petition had called for the investigation and cancellation of NIPCO Plc’s gas distribution licences covering Lagos, Ogun, Oyo and Osun States, as well as the Lagos and Lekki Free Trade Zones. It also sought a public hearing on the matter.

The Sub-Committee, which was granted a 14-day extension on October 26, 2026, to conclude its assignment, announced its decision following its sitting on Thursday.

Speaking on the outcome, Chairman of the Sub-Committee, Hon. Peter Aniekwe, clarified that the issuance and regulation of gas distribution licences fall within the statutory mandate of the NMDPRA under the Petroleum Industry Act.

He, however, reaffirmed the commitment of the National Assembly to continue exercising its oversight responsibilities over the licensing process in the public interest.

Aniekwe disclosed that the NMDPRA had committed to completing and rolling out gas distribution licensing in the fourth quarter of 2026, assuring that the Sub-Committee would closely monitor the process to ensure compliance with the relevant regulatory framework.

He stressed that Nigeria needed a gas market that was open, competitive and safe, noting that investors equally required a transparent and stable regulatory environment to support long-term investment.

According to him, gas remains critical to Nigeria’s energy security and the transition towards more affordable energy alternatives, including cooking gas for households and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) for transportation.

He maintained that the National Assembly would continue to support policies and regulatory frameworks that encourage investment, protect consumers and guarantee that the issuance of licences serves the broader national interest.

The Chairman further assured Nigerians and relevant stakeholders that the House of Representatives remained open to receiving genuine petitions and concerns relating to the gas sector, adding that every petition would be considered on its merits.

Aniekwe expressed appreciation to members of the Sub-Committee and its Secretariat for their diligence and commitment throughout the assignment, formally presenting the Sub-Committee’s decision to dismiss the petition.

World.title: Olaopa Urges Civil Service Commissions To Brace Up For Future Of Work
World.content:
The Chairman of the Federal Civil Service Commission (FCSC), Prof. Tunji Olaopa, has urged civil service commissions to brace up for future of work.

Olaopa spoke on Thursday during the conclusion of the 45th Annual National Council of the Civil Service Commissions of the Federation which held in Asaba, Delta State.

According to Olaopa, civil service commissions must respond to changing professional expectations, generational perspectives and the implications of artificial intelligence.

He urged them to, in collaboration with Offices of the Head of Service, to examine schemes of service, emerging job requirements and the skills needed for effective government.

Noting what would be required in the future of work, he urged civil service commissions to embrace continuous learning, digital competence and the relevant leadership behaviour.

“The standards we enforce, the conduct we tolerate and the contributions we recognise will shape the culture of our institutions”, he said.

While noting the importance of strengthening implementation, communication and peer learning. he said:

” Peer learning, including engagement through the Association of African Public Service Commissions, should help us adapt useful practices to our own circumstance”.

Olaopa said that the leaders of civil service commissions came to Asaba to examine an important question: “How do we reposition our Civil Service Commissions to build a professional, competent, ethical and adaptable civil service that can meet the demands of national development and the expectations of our citizens?”

He said that the theme, “Towards a Future-Ready Civil Service: The Role of Institutional Re-engineering, Reputation Management and Culture Change at the Civil Service Commissions in Nigeria,” provided a framework for answering that question.

He said that the question also challenged leaders of civil service commissions to examine their own institutions, the decisions the decisions they make and the experiences of the people who depend on their services

He said that the meeting was situated within the reform journey that the council pursued together in Katsina in 2024 when it committed to institutional re-engineering and a stronger governance partnership with respective governments and in Umuahia in 2025 when the council examined the FCSC Strategic Plan, 2026–2030, and the imperative of restoring a capable, citizen-centred and accountable civil service.

He added that Asaba was therefore expected to move that conversation forward: to take stock of progress, confront the unfinished business of reform and identify practical steps that Federal and State Commissions could take together.

World.title: Naval Chief Directs Commanders to Secure Nigeria’s Territorial Waters, Protect Economic Prosperity
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS), Vice Admiral Idi Abbas, has directed commanders to remain steadfast in their commitment to securing Nigeria’s territorial waters, combating maritime criminality and protecting the nation’s economic prosperity.

He also charged all commanders to translate the resolutions of the 2026 Chief of the Naval Staff Annual Retreat into tangible operational outcomes.

Speaking at the official closing of the Annual Retreat at Naval Headquarters in Abuja, the CNS said: “I therefore charge all commanders present here to return to your respective Areas of Responsibility with renewed vigour, a sense of purpose and strategic clarity to translate the resolutions of this Retreat into tangible operational outcomes.

“We must remain unyielding in our commitment to securing our territorial waters, combating maritime criminality and protecting the economic prosperity of our dear nation. On my part, I remain dedicated to addressing your logistics, operational and administrative challenges within the ambit of available resources. We will continue to prioritise your needs to ensure you have the requisite manpower, equipment and motivation to effectively dominate your areas of responsibility.”

He, however, pointed out that the true success of the Retreat would not be measured by the brilliant ideas discussed or the strategies proposed, but by the deliberate implementation of the decisions reached at the command level.

According to him, “The depth of the discourse witnessed during the forum reflects our collective resolve, as well as your unwavering passion and commitment to the progress of the Nigerian Navy.

“As I stated in my opening remarks yesterday, this year’s Retreat was convened to provide a vital platform for deep introspection. Accordingly, during the Retreat, we collectively reviewed our operational readiness, identified our challenges, evaluated our strategic objectives and rigorously analysed the evolving security dynamics within our maritime domain.

“More importantly, we were able to identify unique opportunities to improve our operations, enhance our responsiveness, optimise our fleet renewal efforts, strengthen our surveillance capabilities and expand our logistical frameworks.

“With the quality of the strategies proposed during our deliberations, I am optimistic about the future of our Navy. The insights shared and the strategic roadmap we collectively forged here will serve as a compass for years to come.”

Vice Admiral Abbas expressed confidence that the objectives of this year’s Retreat had been fully achieved.

World.title: Orania’s lone EFF voter becomes a social media sensation – again!
World.content:
Orania's lone voter has become a social media sensation. Images via X

Not for the first time, Orania has recorded a lone EFF voter during an Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) election.

According to voter results, the Afrikaner-only town, which falls under the Northern Cape’s Thembelihle Municipality, received an overwhelming majority led by the Freedom Front Plus party, led by Pieter Groenewald.

ORANIA’S EFF VOTER GOES VIRAL

As with what occurred in 2024 during the general elections, an individual exercised their democratic right to vote – for the EFF at the local government elections – at the Orania Town Hall voter station.



The voter results for the Afrikaner-only vote were released to the public and revealed an unmistakable lead for the conservative Afrikaans party, Freedom Front Plus.

Here’s a look at the results.

DA – 44

ACDP – 5

The single individual who voted for the EFF – whose identity remains unknown – quickly became a social media sensation.

Our fighter in Orania is consistent 👌🏽💃🏽😂 https://t.co/cgsplVrIzJ  November 5, 2026

AFRIKAANS-ONLY TOWN HAS ITS OWN ELECTIONS

While Orania hosted a voter station – and permitted residents to exercise their rights to a democratic vote – it also held its own elections, sans political parties.

Leader Joost Strydom posted on X: “Orania holding its own elections today [4 November]. Zero political parties. All candidates are independent and do not receive any pay for their service to the community.



The self-sufficient town elected members of its Orania Representative Council (OVR) – its highest democratically elected community body – which determines representation in the town’s own governing structure and residents’ interests.

The election marked the inaugural one held under the OVR’s new constitution, which launched in August.

As with IEC elections, voters in Orania must be

18 years old on election day.

Be registered on the town’s voters’ roll.

Voters must also have lived in Orania for more than three months and have the right of residence in the town.

World.title: South African restaurant climbs 20 places in world’s best rankings
World.content:
A South African restaurant has secured a place among the world’s 35 best, giving the country’s fine-dining scene another major international achievement.

Cape Town’s La Colombe has been ranked 35th in The 50 Best Restaurants 2026, as well as earning the title of Best Restaurant in Africa.

The announcement was made at the awards ceremony in Lima, Peru, on Wednesday evening, 4 November.



Executive Chef James Gaag accepted the accolade on behalf of the restaurant’s team.

“We are incredibly honoured to be recognised among the world’s best restaurants. It is a very special moment for the entire team, whose dedication and passion make La Colombe what it is,” said Gaag.

He added that representing Cape Town and South Africa on an international stage was something the team never took for granted.

La Colombe climbs 20 places

The latest ranking marks a significant improvement for the Constantia restaurant, which placed 55th in 2025.

It also represents a return to the top 50 after dropping out of the main ranking last year.

La Colombe previously ranked 49th in 2024, when it was also named Best Restaurant in Africa.



South African restaurants on the world stage

La Colombe was not the only Cape Town restaurant to feature in the 2026 rankings.

FYN secured 65th place, while Salsify at the Roundhouse came in at 71st in the extended list of the world’s top 100 restaurants.

The global ranking brings together leading dining destinations from around the world and recognises the talent and creativity shaping the international restaurant industry.

This year’s top spot went to Spain’s Asador Etxebarri, followed by Gaggan in Bangkok and Alchemist in Copenhagen.

World.title: EFF treasurer stabbed to death near voting station
World.content:
Police have arrested a 35-year-old suspect after an EFF branch treasurer was stabbed to death near a voting station in Polokwane, Limpopo. Image: Pexels

Police have arrested a 35-year-old man following the murder of an Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) branch treasurer near a voting station in Polokwane, Limpopo.

The 31-year-old victim died after a man allegedly stabbed him in the neck at a park opposite Flora Park Comprehensive School at about 05:00 on Thursday, 5 November.

EFF Limpopo provincial chairperson Lawrence Mapoulo confirmed that the deceased was the party’s Flora Park branch treasurer.



Argument turns deadly

Limpopo police spokesperson Brigadier Hlulani Mashaba said an argument broke out between two men who were among a group gathered at the park.

Police believe both men belonged to the same political party.

The argument initially subsided, but the suspect allegedly returned and stabbed the victim in the neck before fleeing.

Emergency services declared the man dead at the scene.

Officers recovered a knife believed to have been used in the attack and later tracked down the suspect.

Suspect to appear in court

The suspect is expected to appear in the Polokwane Magistrate’s Court on Friday, 6 November, on a murder charge.



Mashaba said investigators had yet to establish a motive.

Police continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the murder.

World.title: South African business confidence hits lowest level since 2020
World.content:
South African business confidence has fallen to its lowest level since August 2020, according to a private-sector survey released on Thursday.

The S&P Global South Africa Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) remained at 49.0 in October, unchanged from September.

A reading below 50 indicates deteriorating private-sector business conditions, rather than a contraction across the entire South African economy.



Why is South African business confidence falling?

According to Reuters’ report on the survey, David Owen, principal economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence, identified the sharp decline in business confidence as a particularly concerning finding.

Businesses’ expectations for activity over the next 12 months fell to their lowest level in more than six years, with confidence weakening across every sector surveyed.

That does not mean companies expect business activity to decline throughout 2027. Firms still anticipate growth on average, but their expectations are considerably weaker than before.

Fuel prices and port delays push up costs

Higher fuel prices placed further pressure on businesses, pushing purchase-price inflation to its highest rate since June.

Companies also passed some of these costs on to customers, with the rate of increase in selling prices reaching a four-month high.

Supply-chain disruptions added to the pressure. Businesses reported continued delivery delays, including hold-ups at the Port of Durban.



Output declined for a second consecutive month, recording its sharpest fall since December 2025.

The October survey predates the government’s temporary fuel-levy reductions introduced on 4 November. Whether that relief will improve business sentiment remains uncertain.

Orders fall at home and abroad

New orders declined again in October, although the fall was less pronounced than in September. Export demand also weakened for the first time since May.

For workers and consumers, the findings raise concerns about employment opportunities and household costs.

Businesses facing weaker demand may become more cautious about hiring, while rising operating costs can place additional pressure on prices. However, the survey does not establish how many jobs could be affected or predict future retail price increases.
