Mensaje del Presidente de la República, Santiago Peña, al pueblo paraguayo. https://t.co/RBz6IfFV9L — Santiago Peña (@SantiPenap) November 5, 2026

The dispute is also constitutional. Under the Constitution, Congress must accept or reject a president’s resignation; if it accepts, Peña would become a senator for life, with parliamentary immunity. If the Senate removes him through impeachment, he would lose that protection. A session of Congress called to consider the resignation was suspended for lack of a quorum, so for now Peña formally remains president, according to Argentina’s La Nación.

Peña’s downfall accelerated when his own party withdrew its support. Former President Horacio Cartes, head of the ruling Colorado Party and for years his main political backer, endorsed the impeachment. “We will not side with the plundering of public and private funds and of pensioners,” he said. According to El País, prosecutors announced they were opening proceedings against Peña, and opposition lawmakers expanded a criminal complaint alleging illicit enrichment, money laundering and influence peddling, among other offences, which also targets Economy Minister Óscar Lovera, former Central Bank president Carlos Carvallo and other officials. No formal charges have yet been brought against the president.

The crisis erupted on Tuesday, when the Central Bank took over Ueno Bank, the country’s largest digital bank by customers, over insolvency and irregular loans to companies owned by its owners, the Vázquez Group, and froze its deposits, including hundreds of millions of dollars of public and pension funds. The bank’s president and other executives were detained. Thousands of savers took to the streets of Asunción demanding their savings and the president’s resignation. On Wednesday, Peña signed a law to speed up deposit guarantee payouts and proposed Raúl Vera Bogado to head the Central Bank, but failed to stem the crisis.

Carvallo, whom Peña appointed Central Bank president in 2023, had been chief executive of Ueno Bank, and Peña himself was a shareholder in Ueno Holding until April 2025. On the eve of the takeover, Alliana had publicly distanced himself from the president.

Peña, a 47-year-old economist who took office in August 2023, becomes the second Paraguayan president since the return to democracy in 1989 to face impeachment proceedings reaching the Senate; in 2012, the Senate removed Fernando Lugo in a fast-track process.

World.title: Ibero-American foreign ministers unanimously back Argentina’s Falklands claim
World.content:
Ibero-American foreign ministers unanimously back Argentina’s Falklands claim

5th Thursday, November 2026 - 07:21 UTC Full article

“The Ibero-American community reaffirms, once again, its support for the Argentine Republic,” said Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno

Ibero-American foreign ministers meeting in Madrid unanimously approved a special communiqué backing Argentina’s sovereignty claim over the Falklands and calling on Argentina and the United Kingdom to resume negotiations, on the eve of the Hamburg hearing on the Sea Lion oil project.

The document, approved at the foreign ministers’ meeting held during the 30th Ibero-American Summit of Heads of State and Government, urges both governments to resume talks on the dispute “as soon as possible” and acknowledges Argentina’s “constructive attitude”. The Ibero-American Conference, which brings together the countries of Latin America with Spain, Portugal and Andorra, routinely adopts such a statement at its summits.

“The Ibero-American community reaffirms, once again, its support for the Argentine Republic,” said Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno, who called the issue “a sacred cause for Argentines” and defended the diplomatic route to end what he considers an anachronistic colonial situation.

The backing comes five days before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea holds hearings in Hamburg on November 10 and 11 on the four provisional measures Argentina requested on October 13 to halt Sea Lion, which is being developed by Israel’s Navitas Petroleum and Britain’s Rockhopper Exploration. According to the tribunal’s schedule, Argentina will present on the first day from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. and the United Kingdom from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m.; on the second day, Argentina will speak from 10.30 a.m. to noon and the UK will close from 5.30 p.m. to 7 p.m. Argentina’s agent is Ambassador Mario Oyarzábal. The tribunal’s 21 permanent judges include Argentina’s Frida María Armas Pfirter, its vice-president, while the United Kingdom, which has no judge of its nationality, has chosen British professor Vaughan Lowe as judge ad hoc.

Argentina is not asking the tribunal to rule on sovereignty, but on rights to maritime resources and the environmental obligations set out in the Law of the Sea Convention. Sea Lion is expected to begin development drilling in 2027 and commercial production in 2028.

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has called Argentine attempts to interfere with commercial activity in the area “unacceptable”. According to Infobae, the British government will activate legislation before the end of the year to protect Navitas and Rockhopper from possible Argentine sanctions. London maintains that it will not negotiate sovereignty unless the islanders wish it.

World.title: One dead and more than 2,000 affected by El Niño flooding in the Galápagos
World.content:
One dead and more than 2,000 affected by El Niño flooding in the Galápagos

5th Thursday, November 2026 - 07:14 UTC Full article

Authorities announced repairs to the road linking the airport with the island and the removal of debris

Heavy rains linked to the El Niño phenomenon triggered a flash flood on Santa Cruz island in Ecuador’s Galápagos archipelago overnight from Friday to Saturday, leaving one person dead and more than 2,000 affected, according to local mayor Fanny Uribe. Water reached up to three metres deep in some neighbourhoods of Puerto Ayora, the island’s main town.

After some ten hours of heavy rain in the highlands of Santa Cruz, water rushed down a ravine towards the inhabited coastal areas. “Rescues were carried out using kayaks and Zodiacs, and most people were brought to safety,” said fire chief Freddy López, who estimated the water reached three metres in the La Cascada and La Unión neighbourhoods. There were no alarms: firefighters, Red Cross volunteers and young residents went door to door to wake people, some of whom had to swim out of their homes. Most took refuge in the Puerto Ayora Coliseum. A local foundation says it has identified at least 500 more people affected who are not on the official register because they are staying with relatives.

Authorities announced repairs to the road linking the airport with the island and the removal of debris. Uribe said she was negotiating housing vouchers with the government for families who lost their homes, was preparing to distribute 1,000 food kits and that the relocation of the La Cascada neighbourhood was being studied. Residents have organised community kitchens and aid networks; a fishermen’s foundation is serving three meals a day to some 1,200 people. According to El País, President Daniel Noboa had not commented publicly on the emergency.

The Environment Ministry said no deaths of giant tortoises or wild birds have been reported as a result of the rains. Farmers in the island’s highlands, whose produce largely feeds the local population, fear for their crops.

Santa Cruz, with about 15,000 inhabitants, is the most populated island in the Galápagos, some 1,000 kilometres from the mainland. Ecuador’s National Risk Management Secretariat declared a nationwide red alert for El Niño on September 29, and its effects are expected to peak in December.

World.title: Paraguay seeks to return part of the savings frozen at Ueno Bank within 24 hours
World.content:
Paraguay seeks to return part of the savings frozen at Ueno Bank within 24 hours

5th Thursday, November 2026 - 07:08 UTC Full article

Paraguay’s Senate on Wednesday approved a reform of the deposit guarantee law that would allow customers of Ueno Bank, taken over by the Central Bank on Tuesday, to receive an advance of up to 40 minimum wages, about 121 million guaraníes, within 24 hours of the bank’s resolution. The bill now goes to the Chamber of Deputies, which was due to consider it on Thursday.

The current law set a deadline of 15 days, extendable by a further 15, for the Deposit Guarantee Fund to pay savers at a failed bank. The approved text specifies that customers with loans from the bank will have only overdue instalments deducted, not their entire debt, and that the advance is a payment on account that does not change the total coverage of up to 75 minimum wages, about 228 million guaraníes per depositor. According to the Central Bank, that limit covers 97% of customers. Above that figure, the Social Security Institute, the pension fund, will be paid before large savers. The Senate rejected a proposal to extend the guarantee to all public funds deposited in the bank.

The Central Bank’s interim president, Liana Caballero, who took over after Carlos Carvallo’s resignation, said a first payment would be up to 10 million guaraníes and that depositors would be divided into three tranches, although there are still no dates, locations or requirements. “The operational side is the problem in paying out,” she acknowledged. The Association of Banks of Paraguay backed the advance but urged caution over using the fund to return money from pension funds.

“The priority of the government of Paraguay is and will be to protect with all our strength the fruit of that effort and to provide concrete, rapid and responsible answers,” President Santiago Peña said in a televised address. Peña cancelled his attendance at the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid. The opposition has said it will push for impeachment proceedings against him and Vice President Pedro Alliana.

The Central Bank took over Ueno after its solvency ratio fell to 5.56%, against a minimum of 12%, and it detected irregular loans to companies owned by the bank’s owners, the Vázquez Group. Eight executives were detained, according to the press. The crisis also affects South American football’s governing body, Conmebol, which has US$14 million deposited in the bank, although it says payment of prize money for the Copa Libertadores and Copa Sudamericana finals is not at risk. The Vázquez Group’s media outlets closed, leaving about 300 employees without pay. Groups of savers gathered outside the Central Bank on Wednesday night to demand their deposits.

World.title: Republicans look for culprits after defeat: Speaker of Congress steps aside and Vance points to Iran
World.content:
Republicans look for culprits after defeat: Speaker of Congress steps aside and Vance points to Iran

5th Thursday, November 2026 - 07:05 UTC Full article

Johnson, 54, a congressman from Louisiana, has been Speaker since October 2023, when his colleagues chose him as a consensus candidate after the ousting of his predecessor

Speaker of the US House of Representatives Mike Johnson, a Republican, said he will not seek to continue leading his party in the new Congress, while Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the Republican defeat in Tuesday’s midterm elections, an explanation President Donald Trump called “largely true” even as he defended the conflict.

Johnson, 54, a congressman from Louisiana, has been Speaker since October 2023, when his colleagues chose him as a consensus candidate after the ousting of his predecessor, Kevin McCarthy. The Speaker is third in the presidential line of succession, after the vice president, and has been one of Trump’s most loyal allies in Congress. With the Democratic victory, he will lose the post when the new House convenes on January 3, and Republicans will become the minority.

Johnson told his staff on Wednesday that he will not run to lead Republicans in that new phase. In a letter to colleagues he cited the toll three years in the job have taken on his family. “While the outcome of this midterm is not what we’d hoped and fought for, a new battle is just beginning,” he wrote. Congressmen Jim Jordan, chairman of the Judiciary Committee, and Steve Scalise, the majority leader, have already announced bids to succeed him, in a vote expected next week. Trump called Johnson “fantastic” and said he had not asked him to step aside.

Vance, seen as a contender for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, blamed the defeat on the Iran war and rising gasoline prices. “If you want to argue it was worth it — that losing the Senate for the next six years was worth it — go ahead. But everyone knows why we lost,” he wrote on X. Asked about the post, Trump replied: “I think it’s largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit, short term.” But he defended the war, now more than eight months old: “The Iran thing we had to do, and we continue to do it. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon.”

Republicans have lost at least seven Senate seats and could lose nine if results in Mississippi and Alaska, still being counted, are confirmed, according to El País. In the House, dozens of seats remain to be called, although Democrats have already passed the majority. The result also opens the race within the Republican Party to succeed Trump, who cannot run again in 2028.

World.title: Peru declares an El Niño emergency in nearly three-quarters of the country ahead of the Pope’s visit
World.content:
Peru declares an El Niño emergency in nearly three-quarters of the country ahead of the Pope’s visit

5th Thursday, November 2026 - 07:00 UTC Full article

Peru’s scientific commission on the phenomenon expects the episode to last until June 2027

Peru’s government has declared a two-month state of emergency over the risk of heavy rains linked to the El Niño phenomenon in 1,380 of the country’s 1,891 districts, about 73%, including all the places Pope Leo XIV will visit in northern Peru from November 13. The measure covers districts in all 24 departments and the province of Callao.

Rains in recent days flooded homes and streets, leaving 324 people affected in Tumbes, on the border with Ecuador, and caused flooding in Chulucanas, in the Piura region, where the pontiff lived in 1985 during his first years as a missionary. President Keiko Fujimori cancelled her trip to the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid on Sunday to oversee the response and warned of further rain in Tumbes and Piura on November 7 and 8. In October she had already acknowledged that prevention works might prove insufficient for “an El Niño we have not seen in recent decades”. The declaration allows regional and municipal governments to carry out prevention, response and rehabilitation measures with the National Civil Defence Institute.

The emergency includes all 38 districts of Lambayeque, on the northern coast. The Pope, who holds Peruvian nationality and was bishop of Chiclayo, the regional capital, from 2015 to 2023, will celebrate Mass on Friday 13 at the Pampas de Pimentel, by the Pacific, which organisers expect nearly a million faithful to attend. On Saturday 14 he will celebrate another Mass in Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, in the Andean region of Cajamarca, and visit Zaña to close the jubilee year marking 300 years since the canonisation of Saint Toribio de Mogrovejo. The security operation will involve some 2,500 police, 1,000 soldiers and 6,500 volunteers.

“We expect the Pope’s visit to Chiclayo may coincide with episodes of rain. They will not be heavy rains,” said Grinia Ávalos, director of meteorology at the National Meteorology and Hydrology Service, who forecast temperatures of up to 32 degrees Celsius in Chiclayo, four to five degrees above normal. The regional coordinator for the visit, Jorge Chávez Cresta, said that according to the forecast scenarios, heavy rains would reach Lambayeque after the Pope has left the country, although he said contingency plans were in place. The region suffered severe flooding during the El Niño episodes of 1982-1983 and 1997-1998, and Chiclayo lacks a comprehensive drainage system.

Peru’s scientific commission on the phenomenon expects the episode to last until June 2027. In Ecuador, El Niño rains left one dead and more than 2,000 affected on Santa Cruz island in the Galápagos last week. Leo XIV will visit Uruguay and Argentina before arriving in Peru.

World.title: Milei skips the opening of the Ibero-American Summit and meets Abascal in Madrid
World.content:
Milei skips the opening of the Ibero-American Summit and meets Abascal in Madrid

5th Thursday, November 2026 - 06:49 UTC Full article

It is Milei’s second visit to Madrid in two weeks. On October 21, at a breakfast event, he called Sánchez an “unpresentable dictator” and “corrupt”, and did not meet Abascal on that occasion

Argentine President Javier Milei did not attend the opening of the 30th Ibero-American Summit in Madrid on Wednesday or the dinner hosted by the King and Queen of Spain for the delegations, and that evening met Santiago Abascal, leader of the Vox party, in the middle of the campaign for Spain’s November 29 general election.

Milei arrived in the Spanish capital from Buenos Aires on Wednesday afternoon but did not attend the opening ceremony at the Teatro Real or the gala dinner at the Royal Palace for the heads of the 22 delegations. According to diplomatic sources quoted by El País, the Argentine president had requested, through Spain’s Foreign Ministry, a private audience with King Felipe VI, as other leaders had, but the ministry did not process the request, considering it inappropriate for him to meet the monarch before meeting Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. The Argentine government has not explained his absence.

“President Javier Milei met in Madrid with the deputy and presidential candidate Santiago Abascal,” the Argentine Presidential Office said, sharing a photograph of the meeting. Abascal wrote: “Tonight I met my friend and ally Javier Milei, President of the Argentine Republic, whom I thanked for attending the Ibero-American Summit.”

It is Milei’s second visit to Madrid in two weeks. On October 21, at a breakfast event, he called Sánchez an “unpresentable dictator” and “corrupt”, and did not meet Abascal on that occasion. At the time, the Royal Household said a meeting with Felipe VI must necessarily be accompanied by one with the prime minister. Chilean President José Antonio Kast, also attending the summit, met Abascal this week and received an award from Madrid regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso.

Milei is expected to coincide with Felipe VI and Sánchez on Thursday at the summit’s plenary session, which brings together the countries of Latin America with Spain, Portugal and Andorra.

World.title: Democrats retake control of the US Congress in a heavy blow to Trump
World.content:
Democrats retake control of the US Congress in a heavy blow to Trump

4th Wednesday, November 2026 - 09:09 UTC Full article

CBS News projected a Democratic majority in the House shortly after 10 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday; with dozens of seats still to be decided, Democrats had passed the 218 needed

The Democratic Party on Tuesday regained control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate in the midterm elections, winning in Republican strongholds such as Texas, Ohio and Kansas in a heavy blow to President Donald Trump, who will govern for the remaining two years of his term with Congress in opposition hands.

CBS News projected a Democratic majority in the House shortly after 10 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday; with dozens of seats still to be decided, Democrats had passed the 218 needed. In the Senate, they secured a majority with victory in Iowa and hold at least 53 of the 100 seats, with results in Alaska and Mississippi still pending. According to El País, it is only the seventh time the party in power has lost both chambers in a midterm election.

Democrats won Senate seats in states where they had not done so for decades. In Texas, James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton; in Ohio, Sherrod Brown regained the seat from Jon Husted; in Kansas, Methodist pastor Adam Hamilton became the state’s first Democratic senator in almost a century. They also won in Iowa, with Josh Turek; in Maine, where Troy Jackson defeated Republican Susan Collins, a senator since 1997; in North Carolina, with Roy Cooper; and in South Carolina, with Annie Andrews. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrants, will be the first Muslim senator in US history. Republicans held seats in Florida, Idaho and Montana.

In governor’s races, Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott in Texas and will be the first Hispanic woman to lead the state; Xavier Becerra will be California’s first Hispanic governor since 1875; and Deb Haaland, in New Mexico, the first Native American woman to govern a state. In Florida, Republican Byron Donalds will be the state’s first Black governor.

Trump told Fox News he was “a little surprised” and that the Democrats “did a good job”, attributing part of the defeat to the Iran war and higher fuel prices. He told The New York Times he would accept the results and hoped to reach agreements with the opposition. On his social network, however, he wrote: “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!”, and posted an image of his cap bearing the word “VETO”, a reference to his threat to veto the new Congress’s laws.

With majorities in both chambers, Democrats will be able to block the White House’s legislative agenda and open investigations into the first half of the term. Former president Barack Obama said voters had sent “a clear message” in favour of “a politics that brings people together rather than divides them”. China said it was ready to “keep working” with Washington, and the Kremlin said it expected Trump to maintain his foreign policy. Iran’s parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said “Americans have said no to war”.

Polls had identified the cost of living, corruption and the Iran war as voters’ main concerns, and turnout was at record levels for a midterm election.

World.title: Mexican singer-songwriter Silvana Estrada tapped as LA Philharmonic’s first Latin music chair
World.content:
Mexican singer-songwriter Silvana Estrada will help shape the sound of the Los Angeles Philharmonic as its first creative chair for Latin music, expanding her relationship with the orchestra into a role championing Latin American artists and traditions.

The appointment, announced Wednesday, puts the 29-year-old Latin Grammy winner on an artistic leadership team preparing for music director Daniel Harding’s arrival in the 2027-28 season.

Described in 2024 as “the next Mexican global music star” by Mexico News Daily, Estrada will develop programming across Walt Disney Concert Hall, the Hollywood Bowl and The Ford, an intimate amphitheater in the Hollywood Hills.

Her appointment builds on three years of collaborations with the 107-year-old orchestra. She will also collaborate with guest artists and continue working with Youth Orchestra Los Angeles, the organization’s music education program.

“Latin music is not a single sound,” Estrada said in the Philharmonic’s announcement. “To me, it is the soul of an entire continent, an immense and profound richness woven together across generations, with the power to transcend any border.”

Estrada’s piercing lyricism and deeply soulful storytelling come through in her NPR Tiny Desk concerts in 2021 and 2025. Both performances offer English subtitles, allowing viewers who do not speak Spanish to follow her lyrics.

The first was taped at her family’s instrument workshop in Coatepec, Veracruz, during the COVID-19 pandemic and highlighted in the Mexico News Daily article “Regional Mexican music takes over NPR’s Tiny Desk.”

Estrada grew up in the coffee town of Coatepec surrounded by instruments and musicians in her parents’ workshop.

The second was a deeply affecting four-song set in the famously cramped NPR office space, encompassing heartbreak and a defiant message of hope for women facing violence in Mexico.

NPR’s Anamaria Sayre wrote that Estrada brings audiences to tears without extinguishing hope, adding that “her voice finds a way to bend wounds to her will and become whole.”

Her 2022 album, “Marchita,” helped establish her blend of indie folk, jazz and traditional Mexican influences. She won that year’s Latin Grammy for best new artist and received a Grammy nomination for best global music performance in 2024.

Her self-produced 2025 follow-up, “Vendrán Suaves Lluvias,” brought her six 2026 Latin Grammy nominations, including album of the year. The song “Dime” — described by KUTX in Austin, Texas, as “a deceptively lovely song about post-breakup wild rage” — is up for record and song of the year.

The 27th Latin Grammys will be held Nov. 12 at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, with Estrada scheduled to perform and Puerto Rican actress Roselyn Sánchez hosting for the 10th time.

“Vendrán Suaves Lluvias” emerged from profound loss. Estrada told NPR that her best friend and his younger brother were murdered in Mexico City in 2022, leaving her to navigate grief while touring internationally.

The Philharmonic also named British composer and conductor Thomas Adès its creative chair for new music, succeeding John Adams, and Bronx-born jazz vocalist Samara Joy its creative chair for jazz, succeeding Herbie Hancock.

With reports from EFE and NPR

World.title: Mexico’s 2026 growth outlook improves in Banxico and Citi surveys
World.content:
Economic growth in Mexico in 2026 is expected to be higher than previously predicted, according to the median forecasts of economists and analysts surveyed by the Bank of Mexico (Banxico) and Citi.

Conducted in late October, Banxico’s most recent expectations survey yielded a median economic growth forecast of 1.5% in 2026, up from a prediction of 1.4% in September. Economists and analysts from 40 Mexican and foreign private sector economic research and consulting groups responded to the survey.

Economists consulted by Citi for its latest expectations survey are more optimistic about Mexico’s 2026 growth prospects. Their median forecast is 1.8% growth this year, up from 1.4% in the previous survey. Economists from 36 banks, brokerages and research organizations responded to Citi’s survey, whose results were published on Wednesday.

The range of 2026 growth estimates among the economists surveyed by Citi went from 0.9% to 2.1%.

According to preliminary data published by the national statistics agency INEGI last week, Mexico’s economy grew 1.9% in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the same period of 2025.

The economy contracted in sequential terms in the first quarter of the year, but expanded in both Q2 (+1.4% compared to Q1) and Q3 (+0.9% compared to Q2, per preliminary data).

President Claudia Sheinbaum said last week that construction, including housing and public infrastructure projects, was helping to drive growth. Sheinbaum also noted that the production of electronic products in Mexico — many of which are exported to the United States — was providing momentum to the economy.

Growth outlooks for 2027

The median forecast of economists surveyed by Banxico is that Mexico’s economy will grow 1.83% in 2027. The prediction is up slightly from 1.80% in the central bank’s previous survey.

The median forecast of economists surveyed by Citi is that Mexico’s GDP will increase 1.9% next year, up from a 1.8% prediction in the bank’s previous survey.

Inflation predicted to approach 4% by end of year

The median forecasts for Mexico’s annual headline inflation rate at the end of 2026 were 3.88%, according to the Banxico survey, and 3.90%, per the Citi survey. The Banxico forecast rose by 0.01 percentage points while the Citi forecast was unchanged compared to the bank’s previous survey.

Inflation increased in September for a second consecutive month, reaching an annual headline rate of 3.45%. The headline rate spiked to 3.62% in the first half of October, according to INEGI’s most recent inflation data.

Despite the recent increase in inflation, the Banxico board decided on Thursday to lower the central bank’s benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 6.25%. Just six of the 36 respondents to Citi’s survey predicted that the bank would cut its key rate after its November monetary policy meeting.

What will the USD:MXN rate be at the end of 2026?

The median forecasts for the USD:MXN exchange rate at the end of 2026 were 18.39, according to the Banxico survey, and 18.50, per the Citi survey. The Banxico forecast increased from 17.50 in the previous survey, while the Citi prediction rose from 18.20.

The Bank of Mexico’s closing USD:MXN rate on Thursday was 18.75. That rate represents a depreciation of 9.9% for the peso since Sept. 4, when it closed at 16.89 to the dollar — its strongest level in over two years.

The MND Peso Index™ determined that the peso was undervalued by 0.7% in early October when it was trading at just below 18 to the US dollar.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: United Airlines cancels all its remaining flights to Tulum starting in January
World.content:
United Airlines has announced it will cease operations at Felipe Carrillo Puerto International Airport in Tulum starting early next year, citing market conditions as the cause.

The announcement comes just two weeks after American Airlines revealed plans to halt its Miami-Tulum route, following similar moves by other domestic and international carriers including Aeroméxico, Volaris, Copa and Avianca.

The final flight for the connection from Newark is scheduled for Jan. 2, while service from Houston will conclude on Jan. 4. The withdrawal will not be immediate; rather, it will take effect after the year-end holiday period, in accordance with the published schedule.

According to United, affected passengers will be able to modify their bookings.

“Customers will have the option to change their booking to flights arriving at nearby airports, such as Cancún (CUN)—which is a 1.5 to 2-hour drive away and serves many of the same tourist areas as TQO—or, alternatively, they may request a refund,” United said in a statement sent to the newspaper El Financiero.

United’s departure marks the culmination of a gradual reduction in its operations in Tulum. Prior to announcing the cancellation of its connections from Newark and Houston, the airline had already withdrawn its services from Chicago and Los Angeles, thereby diminishing its presence at the Quintana Roo terminal.

Industry reports interpret the company’s “market conditions” rationale for eliminating the flights as Tulum’s lower-than-expected vacation demand.

Industry analysts cited by Aviación News blame the tourism decline on high hotel prices in the area and weaker-than-expected demand for leisure travel. Other contributing factors include the massive influx of sargassum and increased fees and other charges on foreign tourists.

The combination of factors has reportedly led airlines to reassess the profitability of their operations and shift capacity to other destinations with higher passenger volumes.

In this context, Cancún International Airport – located 130 kilometers north of Tulum – emerges as the primary beneficiary of the reorientation of supply.

In the meantime, Air Canada, WestJet, and Air Transat have announced that they will resume flights for the winter season. Viva Aerobus continues its operations at the terminal with no announced changes, and state-owned Mexicana de Aviación remains the only carrier offering an increased number of flights.

With reports from Reportur

World.title: Finance Ministry blocks accounts of former electoral institute chief and associates
World.content:
Guadalupe Taddei, former president of the National Electoral Institute (INE), and José Alfredo Hernández Casillas, a businessman whose companies received lucrative INE contracts, are reportedly among 25 people who have been added to the Finance Ministry’s Blocked Persons List.

The Finance Ministry’s Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF) announced on Wednesday that 25 individuals and 15 companies “linked to electoral suppliers” had been added to the Blocked Persons List, meaning that financial institutions must freeze their bank accounts. It didn’t name the individuals or companies.

The UIF said in a statement that their inclusion on the list came after the detection of “financial transactions that involve elements of risk and warrant review by the appropriate authorities.”

“Inclusion on the Blocked Persons List is a preventive and precautionary administrative measure and does not imply a definitive determination of liability,” the UIF said. “Individuals included on the list are entitled to defense mechanisms and the right to a hearing provided for in applicable legislation.”

The UIF’s announcement of the additions to the Blocked Persons List came nine days after Taddei resigned as INE president amid allegations of corruption. Thirty other INE officials, including 17 who worked in Taddei’s office, have also recently resigned.

During Taddei’s 2023-2026 tenure at the helm of the electoral authority, companies linked to José Alfredo Hernández Casillas and his brother Raymundo Francisco Hernández Casillas received contracts to supply electoral materials to the INE. The ex-INE president reportedly had a close personal relationship with José Alfredo, with some media outlets speculating that they were romantic partners.

The Reforma newspaper reported that José Alfredo Hernández Casillas’ companies had obtained electoral authority contracts dating back to the time that Taddei presided over the electoral organization of Sonora between 2014 and 2021. Taddei’s “closeness” to Hernández allowed the latter to obtain contracts awarded by high-ranking INE officials, Reforma reported.

In an Oct. 25 statement announcing her resignation, Taddei said she was “aware of the allegations that have circulated in the media and on social media, … including rumors, fabrications, leaks and accounts whose authenticity, context and purpose — as in all cases — must be verified and corroborated.”

“… Each allegation must be examined with evidence and through institutional channels,” she said.

Taddei, Hernández Casillas brothers reported to be on the Blocked Persons List

The newspapers La Jornada and El Universal and various other media outlets reported that Taddei and José Alfredo Hernández Casillas are among the 25 people added to the Finance Ministry’s Blocked Persons List. La Jornada cited “a source with access to the list.”

El Universal reported that Raymundo Francisco Hernández Casillas was also added to the list.

The UIF said that in light of the “elements of risk” it detected in financial transactions, it filed a complaint with the Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR) so that the FGR can conduct “the appropriate investigations and determine, in accordance with the law, any potential [criminal] liability.”

📢 #ComunicadoDePrensa La UIF realiza acciones preventivas sobre personas vinculadas con proveedores electorales. La Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público, a través de la Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera (UIF), incorporó a la Lista de Personas Bloqueadas a 40 personas (25 físicas y 15 morales) vinculadas con proveedores electorales. https://t.co/DcPdyl2TU6 🌐 — Hacienda (@Hacienda_Mexico) November 5, 2026

The Federal Auditor’s Office has already launched its own investigation into allegations regarding the “improper use of public resources” by the INE.

At her morning press conference last Thursday, President Claudia Sheinbaum said that Taddei “betrayed the trust of the people of Mexico” by allegedly acting corruptly during her leadership of the INE.

She also asserted that “two or three” companies that received contracts to supply materials such as ballot papers and ballot boxes to the INE — i.e. companies linked to the Hernández Casillas brothers — didn’t actually produce the materials themselves but rather acted as “intermediaries.”

At the same press conference, Pablo Gómez, head of the Presidential Commission for Electoral Reform and a former UIF chief, made similar remarks.

“The companies mentioned don’t have industrial plants. … They don’t make anything. … They’re intermediaries that win contracts and buy everything or go to printers and print everything,” he said.

In light of the alleged corruption in the awarding of INE contracts to companies linked to the Hernández Casillas brothers, Sheinbaum said last Thursday that “most electoral materials” should be made by Talleres Gráficos de México, a government-run printing agency.

To that end, Sheinbaum said today that her government would present a decree next week to strengthen the agency and its governance.

The president has sought to distance her government and the ruling Morena party from Taddei, who has family links to both. Sheinbaum has said that Taddei’s resignation and the scandal engulfing the INE won’t compromise Mexico’s 2027 elections, which are scheduled to take place on June 6.

With reports from La Jornada and El Universal

World.title: Mexico’s trade surplus with the US jumped 26% in the first nine months of 2026, reaching a record US $184 billion
World.content:
The U.S. trade deficit with Mexico grew at an annual rate of 26.1% during the first three-quarters of the year, reaching a record US $184.019 billion, according to U.S. Census Bureau data cited by El Economista.

The balance resulted from a 20.7% increase in U.S. imports of Mexican products compared to the first nine months of 2025, coming in at nearly US $481.6 billion, well above the nearly US $297.6 billion in U.S. exports to Mexico, a 17.6% year-on-year increase.

Mexico’s exports to the U.S. in September (US $62.2 billion) were also a record and mark the third consecutive month that the value of goods shipped from Mexico to the U.S. surpassed US $60 billion.

Mexico accounted for the largest U.S. goods trade deficit in September (US $28.15 billion, a 40% annual increase) and set a new monthly record, although the nine-month trade deficit with Mexico was the second largest for the United States behind only Vietnam (US $190.9 billion).

While the current U.S. administration has declared that one of its priorities is to reduce its trade deficit with the world (especially China), its trade deficit with Mexico has soared due to elevated purchases of computer equipment.

Meanwhile, the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) reported this week that Mexican foreign trade increased 24.6% in the first half of the year, while also citing the expansion of manufacturing acquisitions by the United States, primarily information processing equipment, servers and electronic components for the construction of data centers and Artificial Intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

U.S. demand for AI-related goods was so significant that it explains Mexico’s entire boom in 2025 and between 75-80% of that recorded thus far in 2026, the IDB said.

Mexico’s performance is part of a regional trend as exports of goods from Latin America and the Caribbean grew above the world average in the first half of 2026, with Mexico leading the way.

According to the IDB, exports from the region rose 19.5% year-on-year from January through June, above the 14.5% increase in global trade, primarily due to increased sales of AI infrastructure equipment in the United States.

The IDB noted that Mexico accounts for 93% of regional exports of data processing equipment, servers and electronic components for the construction of data centers and was responsible for 96% of its rebound last year.

With reports from El Economista and La Jornada

World.title: Mexico in Numbers: How many people are emigrating from Mexico?
World.content:
In a previous “Mexico in Numbers” article, we reported on Intercensal Survey data that showed that almost 1.2 million foreign-born residents lived in Mexico in 2025.

Our focus today is on people who emigrated from Mexico to another country. Once again, the data comes from the 2025 Intercensal Survey results report, which was published by the national statistics agency INEGI in September. It looks at emigration from October 2020 to October 2025.

The emigrants counted by INEGI include Mexicans and people from other countries who were living in Mexico, but emigrated between October 2020 and October 2025. Migrants from many countries have spent time living in Mexico before moving on to another country, often the United States — though INEGI doesn’t specify destination countries of emigrants in the Intercensal Survey results report.

How many people emigrated from Mexico between 2020 and 2025?

INEGI reported that 1,259,978 (almost 1.26 million) people emigrated from Mexico between October 2020 and October 2025.

That number represents an increase of 56.95% compared to the preceding five-year period, during which 802,807 people emigrated from Mexico.

Former U.S. President Joe Biden was in office for most of the October 2020 to October 2025 period. Current U.S. President Donald Trump was in office for most of the preceding five-year period. Biden’s border policies were generally more permissive than those of Trump, although he imposed stricter limits on asylum late in his four-year presidency, causing illegal crossings into the U.S. to fall.

How many emigrants returned to Mexico after leaving the country?

INEGI reported that 150,752 emigrants returned to Mexico after leaving the country between October 2020 and October 2025.

That figure represents just under 12% of all people who emigrated in the five-year period.

INEGI reported that 1,022,728 (1.02 million) people had not returned to Mexico after leaving the country between October 2020 and October 2025.

That figure represents 81.2% of all people who emigrated in the period.

INEGI noted in the Intercensal Survey results report that the number of emigrants who remained abroad and the number who returned to Mexico don’t add up to the total number of emigrants in the period between October 2020 and October 2025 because there is a third “not specified” category. A total of 86,498 emigrants fall into that category.

Which states were the largest sources of emigrants?

More than half of all emigrants were living in just 10 Mexican states before leaving the country between October 2020 and October 2025. Those states are:

Guanajuato: The source of 7.5% of all emigrants between October 2020 and October 2025

Michoacán: 6.8%

Veracruz: 6.4%

Puebla: 6.2%

México state: 6.1%

Oaxaca: 5.7%

Jalisco: 5.2%

Chiapas: 4.7%

Guerrero: 4.2%

Hidalgo: 3.7%

The 10 aforementioned states provided 56.5% of all emigrants from Mexico between October 2020 and October 2025.

The five states that provided the lowest number of emigrants in the five-year period are Baja California Sur (0.3% of the total); Campeche (0.5%); Quintana Roo (0.6%); Colima (0.6%); and Tabasco (0.7%).

Men accounted for over 70% of emigrants between 2020 and 2025

INEGI reported that men accounted for 70.4% of emigrants from Mexico between October 2020 and October 2025, while women accounted for 29.6%.

Over one in five emigrants — 22.5% — were aged between 20 and 24 when they left Mexico.

After the group aged 20-24, the next largest cohorts of emigrants were those aged:

25-29: 19.5% of all emigrants

15-19: 15%

30-34: 14.1%

Thus, 71.1% of all emigrants from Mexico between October 2020 and October 2025 were aged between 15 and 34 when they left the country.

More Intercensal Survey coverage from MND

Explore Mexico News Daily’s full Intercensal Survey coverage via the links below.

By Mexico News Daily chief staff writer Peter Davies (peter.davies@mexiconewsdaily.com)

World.title: MND Local CDMX: A nighttime race, queer musical and medieval masquerade
World.content:
With Día de Muertos firmly in the rearview mirror, we have a couple of weeks before the Christmas season really kicks into high gear. But that doesn’t mean Mexico City is short on ways to keep busy in the meantime.

From a nighttime 10K run through UNAM and a musical celebration of queer identity to a medieval-inspired winter masquerade, the capital has a few quirky surprises up its sleeve this December.

Let’s get into it.

Mexico City’s Rave Run brings a nighttime 10K to UNAM

Runners looking for a different kind of nighttime outing can lace up for the Rave Run by Carrera Nocturna 2026, a 10-kilometer race taking place at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM).

Organized by Emoción Deportiva, the event is scheduled for Saturday, Dec. 19, with the starting gun firing at 7 p.m. at Estadio Universitario in Ciudad Universitaria. The race will follow a circuit through the university campus, offering a unique opportunity to experience one of Mexico City’s most recognizable educational institutions after dark.

The competition, billed as a general 10K, is open to anyone 15 and older. Participants must complete the course within a maximum of 80 minutes, and the top three finishers in both the women’s and men’s divisions will receive awards — but don’t expect big cash prizes.

Registration is limited and costs 749 pesos, while late registration costs 849 pesos.

The entry fee includes a commemorative T-shirt, finisher’s medal, runner number, promotional item, race timing, finish-line photography, water and isotonic drinks along the course, medical assistance (hopefully that won’t be needed) and access to official results.

Date: Saturday, Dec. 19

Location: Estadio Olímpico Universitario

Cost: 749-849 pesos

For more information and to register your spot in the race, visit Emoción Deportiva.

Mexico City’s Gay Choir presents a musical journey of identity and self-actualization

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Teatros Ciudad de México (@teatroscdmx)



Mexico City’s premier queer choir, Coro Gay Ciudad de México, is gearing up for its rendition of “La Misteriosa Flama de la Reina Leona,” a coming-of-age musical journey that chronicles two characters as they navigate childhood, identity and self-acceptance.

The performance is slated to take place Tuesday, Dec. 15 at Teatro de la Ciudad Esperanza Iris in the capital’s Historic Center.

Described by the theater troupe as a “journey through shadows, memories and discoveries,” “La Misteriosa Flama de la Reina Leona” explores the search for a mysterious flame that, despite seeming lost, exists within us throughout our lives.

The production unfolds through two childhood stories: The first follows a girl trying to find her way in a world of giants, while the second centers on a boy who, while leading a parade, discovers the courage to realize the best version of himself. Together, the stories explore imagination, identity, fear and the possibility of growing up without abandoning one’s true self.

More than 100 singers and musicians bring the performance to life, allowing the power of music and storytelling to wade through the sometimes messy worlds of memory, reflection and resistance.

The performance is open to all ages, although children ages 3 and older require tickets. It’s also worth noting that Teatro de la Ciudad Esperanza Iris does not have an elevator.

Date: Tuesday, Dec. 15

Location: Donceles 36, Centro Histórico, Cuauhtémoc, 06010 Ciudad de México

Cost: 253-878 pesos

For more information or to purchase tickets, visit Ticketmaster. You can also check out the Coro Gay Choir on Instagram.

Tierra Mágica Navidad brings medieval fantasy to Mexico City

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Festival de Brujas MX (@festival_de_brujas_mx)

Our next event roundup will focus more heavily on Christmas-themed events, but for now, we’ll start with something truly unique and quirky. If your idea of Christmas involves a little more magic, a touch of medieval fantasy and perhaps a masquerade ball, Tierra Mágica Navidad might just be the event for you.

The family-friendly Christmas festival will take over Doméstico in Colonia Hipódromo on Dec. 12 and 13, transforming the venue into a fantasy-inspired celebration that blends traditional holiday festivities with the atmosphere of an enchanted medieval kingdom.

It’s like “Game of Thrones,” but Bran Stark is a young Santa and Westeros is Mexico City.

Visitors are invited to don their finest medieval or fantasy-inspired garb for a weekend of music, magical characters and festive entertainment. Don’t forget your mask, though, as one of the event’s flagship activities is a themed masquerade ball and mask competition, allowing attendees to show off their most imaginative creations.

The festivities will also include a Christmas-themed bazaar full of seasonal offerings. With its combination of holiday traditions, fantasy-inspired characters and immersive activities, Tierra Mágica Navidad sounds to us like an unusual alternative to the capital’s more traditional Christmas celebrations, and a great way to start the season.

Date: Dec. 12 and 13, 11 a.m. to 8:30 p.m.

Location: Av. Nuevo León 80, Hipódromo, Cuauhtémoc, Ciudad de México

Cost: Free

For more information and to register your free spot, visit Tierra Mágica Navidad on Boletia.

Drew Pittock serves as Mexico News Daily’s features director. He is based in Mexico City. Have an idea for a feature story or unique event in CDMX? Send an email to drew.pittock@mexiconewsdaily.com.

World.title: Navy seizes more than a tonne of cocaine off the coasts of Chiapas and Oaxaca
World.content:
The Navy seized more than a tonne of suspected cocaine in two separate operations off Mexico’s southwestern coast.

Security Minister Omar García Harfuch on Thursday confirmed on social media that the actions occurred off the coasts of Chiapas and Oaxaca, adding that one person was arrested.

According to an official statement, the operations took place during maritime patrol and surveillance in the Pacific Ocean.

In the first operation, naval personnel seized 16 packages containing approximately 629 kilograms of “a substance with characteristics similar to cocaine,” while in a second operation they located another 16 packages with around 520 kilograms.

The Navy reported that the weight of 1,149 kilograms includes the packaging and the actual weight of the narcotics will be confirmed by prosecutors.

The statement said that the economic impact for criminal groups is an estimated 273 million pesos (US $14.5 million). “Each seized shipment is a direct blow to the finances of organized crime: reducing their resources to buy weapons, corrupt and generate violence, and fewer drugs on the streets to poison our youth,” García Harfuch said.

Despite the volume of drugs confiscated, authorities reported the arrest of only one person. “The detainee was informed of his rights and placed at the disposal of the Federal Attorney General’s Office,” the statement said.

The latest operation is part of a series of actions carried out in recent months in the Pacific maritime corridor, specifically off the coasts of Chiapas, Oaxaca, Guerrero and Michoacán. Before it, more than 97 tonnes of cocaine had been seized at sea since Claudia Sheinbaum became president in October 2024.

In October, more than 1.2 tonnes of cocaine were seized and six crew members detained in international waters 366 nautical miles south of Huatulco, Oaxaca, in a joint operation with the U.S. Coast Guard.

In August, more than 4 tonnes of cocaine were seized and 13 people arrested during several Pacific operations off Oaxaca and Chiapas.

The ongoing operations are part of permanent maritime and aerial surveillance actions against international drug trafficking, one of the main issues of cooperation and tension in security matters with the United States.

With reports from Proceso, El Financiero and Aristegui Noticias

World.title: Commonwealth’s US$52.9B List Has No Mining
World.content:
MALAWI · ECONOMY

Key Facts The group The Commonwealth is a club of 56 countries, and Malawi is one of its members.

What happened Its new Investment Platform, a list of projects seeking funds, shows 115 projects worth US$52.9 billion.

Malawi’s stake Malawi could export about US$30 billion of minerals between 2026 and 2040, but none are on the list.

The gap Malawi has three listed projects, all tourism resorts, and the platform has no mining category.

The picture Africa has 86 of the 115 projects, and 16 projects each cost more than US$1 billion.

The Commonwealth, a club of 56 mostly former British territories, put a US$52.9 billion project list in front of investors at its summit this week, and mining is not one of its categories. Malawi, a southern African country with large mineral deposits, has no mining project on it.

For US readers, the gap matters because critical minerals such as rare earths, graphite and uranium are a priority for the US government and its supply chains. Our guide to Malawi’s role in Africa explains the country’s position.

What the Commonwealth Published

Commonwealth leaders met from Sunday 1 November to Wednesday 4 November 2026 in St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda. The Commonwealth Secretariat, the group’s administrative arm, says the summit produced more than US$500 million in partnership and investment announcements.

The Secretariat’s Investment Platform now lists 115 projects from 28 countries, with a combined project cost of US$52.9 billion. When it launched before the summit it carried more than 60 projects worth about US$30 billion from 20 countries.

Where the Money Is Pointed

Africa accounts for 86 of the 115 projects, and 16 projects each cost more than US$1 billion. Energy has 27 projects and transport has 26, followed by agriculture with 14.

The platform sorts projects into 12 sectors, including health, tourism, water, digital and housing. Mining is not among them, and the Secretariat’s launch notice names energy, transport, agriculture, manufacturing and the green economy as its main fields.

Malawi’s Three Projects

Malawi has three projects on the platform, and one of them is a US$150.5 million resort on Mount Mulanje in southern Malawi. The other two are resorts at Golden Sands (US$180.5 million) and Salima (US$559 million).

Neighbouring Mozambique lists 13 projects, the most of any country on the platform. Malawi’s three entries are all in tourism, so no mine or mining-related project appears.

The Mineral Case

The World Bank, the global development lender, estimates that Malawi’s mining could earn about US$30 billion in exports between 2026 and 2040. That is gross export value, not money for the state budget, and the Bank links it to new energy investment and a stronger tax regime.

The minerals in question are those used in batteries and clean energy, such as graphite, rare earths and uranium. Mining projects usually need power and rail links, which the platform does list for other sectors.

What It Means for You

If you follow critical-minerals stocks listed in the US, Canada, Australia or London, nothing on this list changes any project’s funding today. The signal is that financing for mines still has to be found outside this platform.

Travellers and importers need not change plans. Anyone tracking US efforts to secure rare earths and graphite should watch whether donors and lenders build power and rail in Malawi alongside the mines.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the Secretariat will add mining or minerals-related projects before 2027. Some listed projects are marked as to be confirmed, so the total may change.

The size of private financing that miners in Malawi still need is not published on the platform. The World Bank’s export estimate also depends on reforms and energy investment that have not yet happened.

What Is the Commonwealth Investment Platform?

It is an online list of investment-ready projects from developing Commonwealth countries. It shows 115 projects in 28 countries with a combined cost of US$52.9 billion.

Does the Platform List Any Mining Projects?

Its 12 sector categories cover energy, transport, agriculture, health and others, but not mining. All three of Malawi’s listed projects are tourism resorts.

How Much Could Malawi Earn From Minerals?

The World Bank estimates about US$30 billion of mineral exports from 2026 to 2040. That is gross export value, not government income.

Which Malawi Projects Are on the List?

Malawi has three, all tourism resorts: Mount Mulanje, Golden Sands and Salima. Together they are listed at about US$890 million.

World.content:

PARAGUAY · POLITICS

Published Thursday, 5 November, 7:30 p.m. ET · Source: Paraguay's Chamber of Deputies and Senate, President Peña's statement on X

Key Facts Free daily brief — no card needed Get every Latin America story in one morning email We build you a personalized brief around the topics you follow — free for 7 days. Love it? What happened Paraguay's Congress did not accept President Santiago Peña's resignation on Thursday 5 November, so he remains in office.

Why Ruling Colorado Party lawmakers who favoured accepting it walked out, leaving too few members to vote.

What next The Senate is due to resume his trial on Friday; 30 of its 45 members must vote to remove him.

The stakes Removal would cost him a lifetime Senate seat and the legal immunity that comes with it.

Paraguay's president quit on camera, and Congress told him no. Santiago Peña, a conservative who has led the country since August 2023, announced his resignation on Thursday 5 November, but lawmakers never accepted it. He is still president tonight, and the Senate is due to pick up his impeachment trial on Friday.

The crisis began with the failure of Ueno Bank, a lender with about three million customers. For US readers, the fight matters because Paraguay is a major soy and beef exporter and a close South American partner of Washington.

This report updates our earlier coverage of the resignation and the vote that spared the vice president. Those reports expected Vice President Pedro Alliana, the constitutional successor, to be sworn in on Thursday evening, and that did not happen.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 with 35.0 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (55); weakest: future resources (13). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Why Congress Said No

Peña's resignation needed a vote in a joint session of Congress, and the session collapsed. Members of the Colorado Party, Paraguay's ruling conservative party, who wanted to accept it were losing the vote, so they left the chamber and the session lost its quorum, the minimum number of members needed to vote.

The walkout surprised many, because the party had said it would back the impeachment. Its leader, former president Horacio Cartes, had said so in a statement.

The reason is immunity. A Paraguayan president who leaves office normally becomes a senator for life, with protection from prosecution.

The opposition and many ruling-party members chose not to accept his resignation so that the impeachment could go ahead and strip him of that status.

Peña Changes Course

Peña answered in a new message on X, formerly Twitter. “With the impeachment trial continuing, I will appear and exercise my right to a defence,” he wrote.

He promised to supply evidence and said the process should respect the constitution. He also said he would give investigators the information they ask for and asked that savers not be made to wait for the political fight.

“The payment to savers cannot stay pending on what happens to me,” he wrote.

What Is the Senate Deciding?

Paraguay's Chamber of Deputies, the lower house, approved the impeachment accusation unanimously earlier on Thursday, as we reported. In an impeachment, the lower house accuses and the Senate, the upper house, judges.

The Senate took up the case that evening. To remove a president, 30 of the Senate's 45 members must vote yes.

The Senate is due to reconvene on Friday, and the charge is poor performance of his duties in connection with Ueno Bank.

The Bank Behind the Crisis

Ueno Bank is a Paraguayan lender with about three million customers. Paraguay's central bank closed it on Tuesday 3 November, and its customers have been locked out of their money since, as we explained in our first report on the impeachment push.

Critics say Ueno drew large deposits from state bodies during Peña's term. In his statements Peña has avoided admitting responsibility.

What It Means for US Readers

The winners from a clean, quick outcome are investors in Paraguayan soy and beef exporters and the savers waiting to be repaid. The losers from a long fight are those same savers and any business that needs a stable government to sign contracts.

The next test is Friday's Senate session, and the number to watch is 30. If fewer senators vote to remove him, Peña stays in office with a damaged mandate; if 30 or more do, Alliana would take over until August 2028.

What Is Not Known

We do not know how many Colorado lawmakers left the chamber, or what time the Senate will meet on Friday. We have also not confirmed whether Peña will attend in person or send a lawyer.

It is unclear whether Congress could still accept his resignation before the trial ends. We found no reaction yet from the US government or from financial markets.

More: Paraguay news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Santiago Peña still president of Paraguay?

Yes. Congress did not accept his resignation on Thursday 5 November 2026, so he remains in office while the Senate continues his impeachment trial.

How many senators must vote to remove Peña?

Thirty of the Senate's 45 members must vote to remove him. The Senate is due to continue the trial on Friday 6 November 2026.

World.title: Mexico City Borough Counts 350,000 Visitors
World.content:
Candles on the graves of San Andrés Mixquic's cemetery, seen from the roof of the San Andrés Apóstol church, pictured on 2 November 2009. Photo: Thelmadatter / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

Mexico City’s boroughs have closed their books on Day of the Dead, and the biggest crowd count so far comes from Iztapalapa, a borough of Mexico City. It reports about 350,000 visitors to its 10 cemeteries, and no serious incidents.

We follow the festival in our Day of the Dead live hub. The holiday ended on 2 November, so these are closing balances, and every figure is self-reported by local governments.

Iztapalapa, a Mexico City borough, counted about 350,000 visitors at 10 cemeteries, with no serious incidents.

When. 31 October to 2 November 2026; boroughs reported on 2 and 3 November.

Other counts. Coyoacán more than 150,000; Xoco cemetery more than 80,000; Mazatlán 48,325.

Caveat. All figures are self-reported; no citywide or national total has been published.

Iztapalapa Reports 350,000 Visitors

About 350,000 people visited the 10 cemeteries of Iztapalapa, a borough of Mexico City, between 31 October and 2 November 2026, according to the borough. It described its security and public-service operation as a “saldo blanco,” meaning it ended without serious incidents.

Municipal crews removed 116 metric tons of waste. The waste figure was preliminary because the night cleanup of 2 November had not yet been counted.

The borough is led by Aleida Alavez Ruiz, its elected head. Its 10 sites comprise three general and seven neighborhood cemeteries, and the borough also reported 221 water-truck trips to supply cemetery cisterns.

Other Boroughs Report a Similar Calm

Coyoacán, another Mexico City borough, said more than 150,000 people visited its historic centre over the festival weekend. It also reported a saldo blanco.

Officials working with the Administrative Verification Institute (INVEA), a city inspection agency, sealed a property in Cantil del Pedregal, a Coyoacán neighbourhood, where a costume contest for more than 500 people was planned. The borough said the site lacked required civil protection measures and permits, and suspension seals were placed.

Xoco cemetery, in the Benito Juárez borough, drew more than 80,000 visitors by 2 November, according to the borough. It stayed open until 11 p.m. local time that day, which was midnight on 3 November in New York (Eastern Time, ET), and diplomats from nine countries, including Israel, Malaysia and Pakistan, attended.

Mazatlán and Miguel Hidalgo Add Their Counts

In Mazatlán, a port city in Sinaloa state, Mayor Estrella Palacios Domínguez said 48,325 people visited municipal and private cemeteries over the holiday. She reported a saldo blanco and said the days hold a special importance for Mexicans.

In Miguel Hidalgo, a borough of Mexico City, Mayor Mauricio Tabe reported a saldo blanco at the Dolores and Sanctórum cemeteries, which he said could receive about 100,000 visitors in total. The borough’s emergency command center logged 19 non-serious medical cases and one hospital transfer after a visitor suffered a muscle injury slipping between graves.

Tabe also backed a proposed cenotaph, a memorial without remains, at the Dolores cemetery for José Guadalupe Posada, the engraver who created the skeleton figure known as La Catrina. According to the borough, his remains lie in a common grave and can no longer be located, and a civil association has gathered more than 12,000 signatures, though no monument has been announced.

Why the Figures Cannot Be Added Up

The counts come from the boroughs themselves and cover different periods, so they cannot be combined into a citywide total. Iztapalapa’s covers 31 October to 2 November, Coyoacán’s begins earlier in the weekend, and Mazatlán’s covers only the holiday itself.

No consolidated result has been published for the whole city. Pre-holiday visitor projections varied by outlet and were forecasts, not outcomes.

What It Means for US Readers

The crowds were large and the reports were calm, which matters for Americans who plan to visit Mexico City for the festival next year. Treat the local crowd figures as official estimates, not audited counts.

Visitors from abroad were among those attending, including diplomats from nine countries at Xoco cemetery. A calm balance does not remove the usual advice to check local conditions before travelling.

What Is Not Known

No final official citywide visitor count for Mexico City in 2026 has been found, and no federal tourism or economic-impact results for the holiday. All visitor counts and saldo blanco assessments are self-reported by borough and municipal governments.

Iztapalapa’s waste total may change once its final cleanup is counted. We found no report of a violent incident at the cemeteries covered here, which reflects the reports we reviewed, not independent confirmation that none occurred.

More: Mexico news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people visited Iztapalapa’s cemeteries?

About 350,000 people visited its 10 cemeteries between 31 October and 2 November 2026, according to the borough. The figure is the borough’s own estimate.

What does saldo blanco mean?

It is the term Mexican local authorities use for an operation that ends without serious incidents. Boroughs can still record minor medical cases under that label.

Is there a total for all of Mexico City?

No consolidated citywide count has been published in the material we reviewed. Each borough counts visitors over its own dates and by its own method.

World.title: Colombia Rebels Seize Officer María Pantoja
World.content:
Key Facts Who. Colombian Army sub-lieutenant María Camila Pantoja Hernández was abducted in Saravena, Arauca, near Venezuela, on Wednesday 4 November 2026.

Claim. The ELN (National Liberation Army), a Colombian guerrilla group, says its Eastern War Front seized her and that she is well.

Army. The Army attributes the kidnapping to the ELN and says search protocols are active.

Unknown. Her location, her health and any ELN demands are not known.

Status. As of 5 November 2026, 23:00 GMT

Colombia’s ELN guerrilla group says it kidnapped Army sub-lieutenant María Camila Pantoja in Saravena, a town in Arauca near the Venezuelan border. The Army says it has activated search protocols, and rescue efforts are under way.

The ELN, or National Liberation Army, is one of Colombia’s largest guerrilla groups and is designated a terrorist organisation by the United States. Arauca is a Colombian province on the Venezuelan frontier, where armed groups are active.

Free daily brief — no card needed Get every Colombia story in one morning email We build you a personalized brief around the topics you follow — free for 7 days. Love it? Your first month after that is US$1. Start my free brief Yes, email me my free daily brief — I can unsubscribe any time.

Ms Pantoja was taken on the afternoon of Wednesday 4 November 2026, in the urban area of Saravena. The ELN claimed the abduction on Thursday 5 November in a video and a written communiqué.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Colombia ranks 6th of 14 with 51.1 points. Strongest pillar: military means (91); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (28). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What We Know

Pantoja Hernández is a subteniente, or sub-lieutenant, attached to the Army’s 18th Cavalry Group. Military sources say she was assigned to intelligence units, a detail we could not independently confirm.

Saravena is a town in Arauca, an oil-producing province that Colombia shares with Venezuela. Armed groups and the Army have contested the area for years.

The Army’s official name for her unit is Grupo de Caballería Mediano No. 18, or Medium Cavalry Group No. 18. Military sources say she was carrying out tasks assigned by her superiors.

Reports say two armed men on a motorcycle intercepted her in the town centre on Wednesday. The Ombudsman’s Office, Colombia’s state human rights watchdog, says she was wearing civilian clothes.

The office, led by Iris Marín Ortiz, demanded her immediate release. It cited Early Warning Alert 014-25, a formal risk notice it issued for Arauca in October 2025.

The Ombudsman’s Office is an independent state body that monitors human rights. It also issues early warnings when armed groups threaten civilians in a region.

The alert, issued on 20 October 2025, warned of fighting in Arauca between the ELN and FARC dissidents, former rebels who rejected the 2016 peace deal. It did not single out this case.

On Thursday the ELN published a video and communiqué claiming the abduction. It says its Eastern War Front, a regional command, carried out an “urban search and control action”.

The group says she is well and that her rights will be respected, though it ties this to the realities of war in the region. It holds the armed forces responsible for “any rescue attempt that puts her life at risk”.

The ELN formed in 1964 and has fought the Colombian state for decades. It stayed outside the 2016 peace deal that disarmed the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), once the country’s largest rebel group.

The Army attributes the kidnapping to the ELN’s Domingo Laín Sáenz front, a unit within the Eastern War Front. It has activated search protocols, with the Navy, the Aerospace Force and the National Police involved.

The kidnapping follows an Army offensive against the ELN, including recent bombings of the group’s camps. President Abelardo De La Espriella leads the government that is pressing that campaign.

What Is Not Known

As of Thursday night, neither the Army nor the ELN has said where Ms Pantoja is being held. The ELN has published no demands or conditions for her release.

Some Colombian military sources fear the group may take her across the border into Venezuela. That concern is unconfirmed, and we have seen no evidence that she has left Colombia.

The ELN has not said how long it plans to hold her. Nor has it said whether it will release proof of her condition.

Her condition rests only on the ELN’s own statement. Her military role, including the intelligence assignment, rests on military sources alone.

Casa de Nariño, the presidential palace in Bogotá. (File photo) photo. The Casa de Nariño, Colombia's presidential palace, Bogotá. Photo: Mriobomorales, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

The US government designates the ELN a terrorist organisation. Arauca is a conflict zone, and the Army is now running search operations there.

The ELN has long been reported to operate on both sides of the Venezuelan border. Military sources told Colombian media the Army is manoeuvring to prevent a move across that frontier.

Travellers should follow their own government’s advisories before any trip near the Venezuelan border. Those advisories change as security conditions change.

For US readers, the case is a reminder of the risks armed groups pose near the Venezuelan border. We will update this story when the Army or the ELN release new information.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is María Camila Pantoja?

She is an Army sub-lieutenant attached to the Army’s 18th Cavalry Group. Military sources say she served in intelligence units, and she was kidnapped in Saravena on 4 November 2026.

Who is holding her?

The ELN, one of Colombia’s largest guerrilla groups, claimed the kidnapping on 5 November. The Army attributes the kidnapping to the ELN’s Domingo Laín Sáenz front.

Where is she now?

Her location is unknown. The Army has activated search protocols, and some military sources fear she could be taken into Venezuela, which is unconfirmed.

Is it safe to travel to Arauca?

Arauca is a conflict zone near the Venezuelan border, and the ELN is active there. Travellers should check their own government’s advisories before planning any trip.

The next signals to watch are any proof of life, any ELN conditions and the Army’s account of the search. Until then, the open questions above remain open.

Sources: Colombian Army statement (5 November 2026); ELN video and communiqué (5 November 2026); Defensoría del Pueblo (Ombudsman’s Office) statement. World.content:
CASABLANCA · Culture

French pop star GIMS plays Casablanca on Saturday 7 November, the city’s video art festival runs from 10 to 14 November and Moroccan singer Manal fills the Complexe Mohammed V on 21 November. Here is what we could confirm for the rest of the month.
